bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第179卷卷第一百七十九

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 179, Volume Number One Hundred Seventy-Nine
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 179

sentences.zh: 【隋紀三】　起上章灘，盡昭陽大淵獻，凡四年。

translations.literal: [Sui Records 3] From the Shangzhangtan year through the Zhaoyang Dayuanxian year, four years in all.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Records 3, from the Shangzhangtan year through the Zhaoyang Dayuanxian year—a span of four years.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，熙州人李英林反。

translations.literal: Spring, second month: Li Yinglin of Xizhou rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the second month, Li Yinglin of Xizhou rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛卯，以揚州總管司馬河內張衡為行軍總管，帥步騎五萬討平之。

translations.literal: Third month, on the day xinmao, Zhang Heng of Henei, chief administrator under the Yangzhou military governor, was made campaigning commander and led fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack and pacify the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day xinmao, Zhang Heng of Henei—chief administrator under the Yangzhou military governor—was appointed campaigning commander and led fifty thousand foot soldiers and cavalry to suppress and pacify the revolt.

sentences.zh: 賀若弼復坐事下獄，上數之曰：「公有三太猛：嫉妒心太猛，自是、非人心太猛，無上心太猛。

translations.literal: He Ruobi was again imprisoned for an offense. The emperor reckoned him up, saying: "You have three excessive fiercenesses: your jealousy is too fierce, your insistence on your own right and others' wrong is too fierce, and your lack of deference to superiors is too fierce.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruobi was imprisoned again over some offense. The emperor enumerated his faults: "You have three fatal excesses: jealousy runs too deep in you, you insist too stubbornly on being right and everyone else wrong, and you show far too little deference to your superiors.

sentences.zh: 」既而釋之。

translations.literal: " He was then released.
translations.idiomatic: " He was soon released.

sentences.zh: 他日，上謂侍臣曰：「弼將伐陳，謂高熲曰：『陳叔寶可平也。

translations.literal: Another day the emperor said to his attendants: "When Bi was about to campaign against Chen, he said to Gao Yong: 'Chen Shubao can be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor told his attendants: "When Bi was preparing to attack Chen, he said to Gao Yong: 'Chen Shubao can be subdued.

sentences.zh: 不作高鳥盡、良弓藏邪？

translations.literal: Will you not do as they say—when the high birds are gone, the good bows are stored away?'
translations.idiomatic: Surely you won't treat me like the proverb says—when the high birds are gone, the good bows are put away?'

sentences.zh: 』熲云『必不然。

translations.literal: ' Yong replied: 'Surely not.
translations.idiomatic: ' Yong answered: 'Of course not.

sentences.zh: 』及平陳，遽索內史，又索僕射。

translations.literal: ' After Chen was pacified, he immediately demanded the post of Director of the Secretariat, and then demanded that of Vice Premier.
translations.idiomatic: ' But once Chen was subdued, he immediately demanded the Secretariat directorship, then the vice-premiership as well.

sentences.zh: 我語熲曰：『功臣正宜授勳官，不可預朝政。

translations.literal: ' I told Yong: 'Meritorious ministers should rightly receive honorary titles; they must not meddle in court politics.
translations.idiomatic: ' I told Yong: 'Men who have earned merit should receive honorary posts—not seats in government.

sentences.zh: 』弼後語熲：『皇太子於己，出口入耳，無所不盡。

translations.literal: ' Later Bi said to Yong: 'The Crown Prince holds nothing back with me—what goes out of his mouth enters my ear, and he withholds nothing.
translations.idiomatic: ' Later Bi told Yong: 'The Crown Prince confides in me completely—nothing he says stays between us.

sentences.zh: 公終久何必不得弼力，何脈脈邪！

translations.literal: Why must you in the end necessarily not get Bi's support? Why so furtive and lingering!'
translations.idiomatic: In time you'll surely need my help—why play these secretive games?'

sentences.zh: 』意圖廣陵，又圖荊州，皆作亂之地，意終不改也。

translations.literal: ' He set his sights on Guangling and also on Jingzhou—both regions prone to rebellion—and his intent never changed.
translations.idiomatic: ' He was fixated on Guangling and Jingzhou—both notorious centers of unrest—and he never changed.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬戌，突厥達頭可汗犯塞，詔命晉王廣、楊素出靈武道，漢王諒、史萬歲出馬邑道以擊之。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on the day renxu, Tardu Khan of the Turks violated the frontier. An edict ordered Prince of Jin Yang Guang and Yang Su to advance by the Lingwu route, and Prince of Han Yang Liang and Shi Wansui to advance by the Mayi route to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the day renxu, Tardu Khan of the Turks raided the border. The emperor ordered Prince Jin Yang Guang and Yang Su out by the Lingwu route, and Prince Han Yang Liang and Shi Wansui by the Mayi route to drive him back.

sentences.zh: 長孫晟帥降人為秦州行軍總管，受晉王節度。

translations.literal: Changsun Sheng led surrendered men as campaigning commander of Qinzhou, subject to the Prince of Jin's command.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Sheng took command of surrendered troops as campaigning commander of Qinzhou, under Prince Jin's orders.

sentences.zh: 晟以突厥飲泉，易可行毒，因取諸藥毒水上流，突厥人畜飲之多死，於是大驚曰：「天雨惡水，其亡我乎！

translations.literal: Sheng, knowing the Turks drank from the spring and that poison could easily be applied, took various drugs and poisoned the upstream water. Many Turks—men and livestock—drank and died. Thereupon they were greatly alarmed and said: "Heaven has rained foul water—is it destroying us?
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the Turks drank from a spring where poison could be introduced upstream, Sheng drugged the headwaters. Turk men and beasts drank and died in large numbers. Terror spread: "Heaven has sent poisoned rain—are we being destroyed?

sentences.zh: 」因夜遁。

translations.literal: " They fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: " That night they fled.

sentences.zh: 晟追之，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: Sheng pursued and beheaded more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng gave chase and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 史萬歲出塞，至大斤山，與虜相遇。

translations.literal: Shi Wansui went beyond the frontier to Mount Dajin and encountered the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wansui crossed the border to Mount Dajin and met the enemy there.

sentences.zh: 達頭遣使問：「隋將為誰？

translations.literal: Tardu sent an envoy to ask: "Who is the Sui general?
translations.idiomatic: Tardu sent a messenger to ask: "Who commands the Sui forces?

sentences.zh: 」候騎報：「史萬歲也。

translations.literal: " The scout riders reported: "Shi Wansui."
translations.idiomatic: " The scouts replied: "Shi Wansui."

sentences.zh: 」突厥復問：「得非敦煌戍卒乎？

translations.literal: " The Turks asked again: "Could he be the Dunhuang garrison soldier?
translations.idiomatic: " The Turks pressed: "Isn't he the man from the Dunhuang garrison?

sentences.zh: 」候騎曰：「是也。

translations.literal: " The scouts said: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: " The scouts confirmed: "Yes, that's him."

sentences.zh: 」達頭懼而引去。

translations.literal: " Tardu, afraid, withdrew his forces.
translations.idiomatic: " Tardu was terrified and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 萬歲馳追百餘里，縱擊，大破之，斬數千級；

translations.literal: Wansui galloped in pursuit for more than a hundred li, let loose an attack, and routed them thoroughly, beheading several thousand;
translations.idiomatic: Wansui chased them hard for more than a hundred li, smashed their line, and took several thousand heads;

sentences.zh: 逐北，入磧數百里，虜遠遁而還。

translations.literal: Pursuing the fleeing northerners, he entered the desert for several hundred li; when the enemy had fled far off, he returned.
translations.idiomatic: He drove the fleeing northerners deep into the desert for hundreds of li before turning back once they had scattered beyond reach.

sentences.zh: 詔遣長孫晟復還大利城，安撫新附。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Changsun Sheng back to Dali Fort to pacify the newly submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Changsun Sheng back to Dali Fort to settle the newly submitted tribes.

sentences.zh: 達頭復遣其弟子俟利伐從磧東攻啟民，上又發兵助啟民守要路；

translations.literal: Tardu again sent his nephew's son Helifa to attack Qimin from east of the desert; the emperor also dispatched troops to help Qimin hold the key passes;
translations.idiomatic: Tardu again sent his nephew Helifa to strike Qimin from east of the desert; the emperor also sent troops to help Qimin hold the critical passes;

sentences.zh: 俟利伐退走入磧。

translations.literal: Helifa retreated and fled into the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Helifa fell back into the desert.

sentences.zh: 啟民上表陳謝曰：「大隋聖人可汗憐養百姓，如天無不覆，地無不載。

translations.literal: Qimin submitted a memorial expressing gratitude: "The Sage Khan of Great Sui pities and nurtures the people, like heaven covering all and earth bearing all.
translations.idiomatic: Qimin sent a memorial of thanks: "The Sage Khan of Great Sui nurtures his people as heaven covers all and earth bears all.

sentences.zh: 染干如枯木更葉，枯骨更肉，千世萬世，常為大隋典羊馬也。

translations.literal: Ran'gan is like withered wood putting forth new leaves, dry bones growing flesh again; for a thousand generations and ten thousand ages I shall forever raise sheep and horses for Great Sui.
translations.idiomatic: I, Ran'gan, am like dead wood sprouting new leaves, bare bones clothed in flesh again; for ten thousand generations I shall herd sheep and horses for Great Sui.

sentences.zh: 」帝又遣趙仲卿為啟民築金河、定襄二城。

translations.literal: " The emperor also sent Zhao Zhongqing to build the two fortresses Jinhe and Dingxiang for Qimin.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor also dispatched Zhao Zhongqing to build the Jinhe and Dingxiang fortresses for Qimin.

sentences.zh: 秦孝王俊久疾，未能起，遣使奉表陳謝。

translations.literal: Prince Xiaojun of Qin had long been ill and could not rise; he sent an envoy submitting a memorial of apology.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qin Xiaojun had been bedridden with illness for a long time and sent an envoy with a memorial of apology.

sentences.zh: 上謂其使者曰：「我戮力創茲大業，作訓垂范，庶臣下守之。

translations.literal: The emperor said to his envoy: "I exerted my strength to create this great enterprise, established teachings to be a lasting model, hoping my subjects would uphold them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the envoy: "I labored to build this empire and set an example for those who come after, expecting my officials to honor that legacy.

sentences.zh: 汝為吾子，而欲敗之，不知何以責汝！

translations.literal: You are my son, yet you wish to ruin it—I do not know how to hold you accountable!
translations.idiomatic: You are my own son, yet you would throw it away—I scarcely know how to answer for you!

sentences.zh: 」俊慚怖，疾遂篤，乃復拜俊上柱國；

translations.literal: " Jun was ashamed and fearful; his illness then grew severe, and the emperor again invested Jun as Honorary Pillar of State;
translations.idiomatic: " Jun was stricken with shame and dread; his illness worsened, and the emperor restored him as Honorary Pillar of State;

sentences.zh: 六月，丁丑，俊薨。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on the day dingchou, Jun died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day dingchou, Jun died.

sentences.zh: 上哭之，數聲而止。

translations.literal: The emperor wept for him, stopping after a few cries.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept briefly and stopped.

sentences.zh: 俊所為侈麗之物，悉命焚之。

translations.literal: All the lavish objects Jun had made were ordered burned.
translations.idiomatic: Every luxurious thing Jun had accumulated was ordered burned.

sentences.zh: 王府僚佐請立碑，上曰：「欲求名，一卷史書足矣，何用碑為！

translations.literal: The prince's staff requested a stele; the emperor said: "If one seeks a name, a single scroll of historical writing suffices—what need for a stele!
translations.idiomatic: His staff asked to erect a stele; the emperor said: "If you want a name, one page in the histories is enough—why need a stone monument?

sentences.zh: 若子孫不能保家，徒與人作鎮石耳！

translations.literal: If descendants cannot preserve the family, it would only serve others as a door-weight!
translations.idiomatic: If your descendants cannot hold the house together, the stone will only anchor someone else's gate!"

sentences.zh: 」俊子浩，崔妃所生也；

translations.literal: " Jun's son Hao was born to Consort Cui;
translations.idiomatic: Jun's son Hao was born to Consort Cui;

sentences.zh: 庶子曰湛。

translations.literal: The son by a concubine was Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: His son by a concubine was Zhan.

sentences.zh: 群臣希旨，奏稱：「漢之栗姬子榮、郭后子強皆隨母廢，今秦王二子，母皆有罪，不合承嗣。

translations.literal: The ministers, seeking to please, memorialized: "In Han, Liu Rong son of Lady Li and Liu Qiang son of Empress Guo were both deposed along with their mothers; now the Prince of Qin's two sons—both their mothers had committed offenses—are unfit to inherit.
translations.idiomatic: Flattering the emperor, ministers reported: "In Han times, Liu Rong son of Lady Li and Liu Qiang son of Empress Guo lost succession when their mothers fell; both sons of Prince Qin have mothers guilty of offenses and should not inherit."

sentences.zh: 」上從之，以秦國官為喪主。

translations.literal: " The emperor agreed and made a Qin-state official the chief mourner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, making a Qin official chief mourner instead.

sentences.zh: 初，上使太子勇參決軍國政事，時有損益，上皆納之。

translations.literal: Initially the emperor had Crown Prince Yong participate in deciding military and state affairs; when he offered improvements or cuts, the emperor always accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor had Crown Prince Yong take part in military and state affairs; the emperor accepted his suggestions whenever he offered them.

sentences.zh: 勇性寬厚，率意任情，無矯飾之行。

translations.literal: Yong's nature was generous and broad; he followed his inclinations and feelings without pretense.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was open and generous by nature, following his own inclinations without affectation.

sentences.zh: 上性節儉，勇嘗文飾蜀鎧，上見而不悅，戒之曰：「自古帝王未有好奢侈而能久長者。

translations.literal: The emperor's nature was frugal; Yong once had Shu armor decorated with patterns; the emperor saw it and was displeased, admonishing him: "From antiquity no emperor who loved luxury has been able to endure long.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lived simply; Yong once had Shu armor ornamented with designs. The emperor disapproved and warned him: "No emperor in history who loved extravagance lasted long.

sentences.zh: 汝為儲後，當以儉約為先，乃能奉承宗廟。

translations.literal: You, as heir apparent, must put frugality first—only then can you uphold the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: As heir, you must make thrift your first duty if you hope to serve the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 吾昔日衣服，各留一物，時復觀之以自警戒。

translations.literal: I have kept one item from each of my old garments and from time to time look at them to warn myself.
translations.idiomatic: I kept one piece from each set of old clothes and look at them now and then to remind myself.

sentences.zh: 恐汝以今日皇太子之心忘昔時之事，故賜汝以我舊所帶刀一枚，並菹醬一合，汝昔作上士時常所食也。

translations.literal: Fearing that with the heart of Crown Prince today you might forget former times, I give you an old sword I once wore and a jar of pickled sauce—what you regularly ate when you were a Senior Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that as Crown Prince you'll forget humbler days. So I give you the sword I once wore and a jar of pickled sauce—the food you ate as a senior gentleman.

sentences.zh: 若存記前事，應知我心。

translations.literal: If you preserve memory of former things, you should know my heart.
translations.idiomatic: If you remember where you came from, you'll understand what I mean."

sentences.zh: 後遇冬至，百官皆詣勇，勇張樂受賀。

translations.literal: Later, on the winter solstice, all officials went to Yong's residence; Yong set out music and received congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at the winter solstice, officials flocked to Yong's residence; he held music and accepted their congratulations.

sentences.zh: 上知之，問朝臣曰：「近聞至日內外百官相帥朝東宮，此何禮也？

translations.literal: The emperor learned of it and asked court ministers: "I recently heard that on the solstice officials inside and outside all led one another to attend upon the Eastern Palace—what sort of rite is this?
translations.idiomatic: Learning of this, the emperor asked his ministers: "I've heard that at the solstice officials inside and outside the court all went together to the Eastern Palace—what kind of ceremony is that?

sentences.zh: 」太常少卿辛但對曰：「於東宮，乃賀也，不得言朝。

translations.literal: " Minor Director of Rituals Xin Dan replied: "At the Eastern Palace it is congratulation, not properly called attendance at court.
translations.idiomatic: " Director of Rituals Xin Dan answered: "At the Eastern Palace it was congratulations, not a formal court audience.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「賀者正可三數十人，隨情各去，何乃有司徵召，一時普集！

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Congratulations might rightly involve a few dozen people going as each sees fit—why did the offices summon them and gather everyone at once!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "A few dozen might offer congratulations as they please—why did the offices summon everyone at once?

sentences.zh: 太子法服設樂以待之，可乎？

translations.literal: The crown prince in full ceremonial dress setting out music to wait for them—is that permissible?
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince in full ceremonial dress with music laid on—is that acceptable?

sentences.zh: 」因下詔曰：「禮有等差，君臣不雜。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he issued an edict: "Rites have gradations; lord and subject must not be mixed.
translations.idiomatic: " He then issued an edict: "Rites observe rank; subjects must not mingle with the sovereign as equals.

sentences.zh: 皇太子雖居上嗣，義兼臣子，而諸方岳牧正冬朝賀，任土作貢，別上東宮；

translations.literal: The crown prince, though occupying the position of senior heir, in duty is also a subject; yet regional governors offering winter solstice greetings and regional tribute separately presented to the Eastern Palace—
translations.idiomatic: Though heir apparent, the Crown Prince is still a subject; yet regional governors sent solstice greetings and tribute separately to the Eastern Palace—

sentences.zh: 事非典則，宜悉停斷！

translations.literal: Such matters are not canonical precedent and should all be halted!
translations.idiomatic: This is irregular and must cease entirely!"

sentences.zh: 」自是恩寵始衰，漸生猜阻。

translations.literal: " From this his grace and favor began to wane, and suspicion and obstruction gradually arose.
translations.idiomatic: From then his favor began to fade, and mistrust grew between them.

sentences.zh: 勇多內寵，昭訓雲氏尤幸。

translations.literal: Yong had many favored women within; Lady Yun of Zhaoxun rank was especially favored.
translations.idiomatic: Yong kept many favored concubines; Lady Yun, of Zhaoxun rank, was his favorite.

sentences.zh: 其妃元氏無寵，遇心疾，二日而薨，獨孤後意有他故，其責望勇。

translations.literal: His principal consort, of the Yuan clan, was without favor; she encountered heart illness and died within two days. Empress Dugu suspected another cause and blamed Yong for it.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Yuan had fallen out of favor; she took ill with heart trouble and died within two days. Empress Dugu suspected foul play and blamed Yong.

sentences.zh: 自是雲昭訓專內政，生長寧王儼、平原王裕、安成王筠；

translations.literal: From this Lady Yun Zhaoxun monopolized domestic affairs; she bore Princes Yan of Changning, Yu of Pingyuan, and Jun of Ancheng;
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Lady Yun Zhaoxun ruled the inner household. She bore Prince Yan of Changning, Prince Yu of Pingyuan, and Prince Jun of Ancheng;

sentences.zh: 高良娣生安平王嶷、襄城王恪；

translations.literal: Lady Gao, liangdi rank, bore Princes Ni of Anping and Ke of Xiangcheng;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Gao bore Prince Ni of Anping and Prince Ke of Xiangcheng;

sentences.zh: 王良媛生高陽王該、建安王韶；

translations.literal: Lady Wang bore Princes Gai of Gaoyang and Shao of Jian'an;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang bore Prince Gai of Gaoyang and Prince Shao of Jian'an;

sentences.zh: 成姬生穎川王煚；

translations.literal: Lady Cheng bore Prince Jiong of Yingchuan;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cheng bore Prince Jiong of Yingchuan;

sentences.zh: 後宮生孝實、孝范。

translations.literal: Women of the rear palace bore Xiaoshi and Xiaofan.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser palace women bore Xiaoshi and Xiaofan.

sentences.zh: 後彌不平，頗遣人伺察，求勇過惡。

translations.literal: The empress grew increasingly resentful and sent people to spy, seeking Yong's faults and misdeeds.
translations.idiomatic: The empress grew more bitter and sent agents to watch for Yong's missteps.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣，彌自矯飾，唯與蕭妃居處，後庭有子皆不育，後由是數稱廣賢。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Yang Guang, on the contrary, cultivated self-restraint; he lived only with Consort Xiao; sons born in the rear quarters were all not raised to maturity; because of this the empress repeatedly praised Guang's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin Yang Guang, by contrast, practiced careful self-restraint; he lived alone with Consort Xiao and let no sons from the rear quarters survive—so the empress often praised his virtue.

sentences.zh: 大臣用事者，廣皆傾心與交。

translations.literal: Powerful ministers—Guang winned them all over and befriended them.
translations.idiomatic: Every influential minister Guang cultivated with deliberate warmth.

sentences.zh: 上及後每遣左右至廣所，無貴賤，廣必與蕭妃迎門接引，為設美饌，申以厚禮；

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor or empress sent attendants to Guang's residence, regardless of rank, Guang and Consort Xiao always met them at the gate, set out fine fare, and treated them with utmost courtesy;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor or empress sent attendants to Guang—high or low—he and Consort Xiao met them at the gate, served fine food, and lavished attention on them;

sentences.zh: 婢僕往來者，無不稱其仁孝。

translations.literal: Servants and attendants coming and going all praised his benevolence and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Every servant who passed through praised his kindness and filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 上與後嘗幸其第，廣悉屏匿美姬於別室，唯留老醜者，衣以縵彩，給事左右；

translations.literal: The emperor and empress once visited his residence; Guang hid all beautiful women in separate chambers, keeping only old and homely ones dressed in plain silk to attend nearby;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor and empress visited, Guang hid every beautiful woman in a side room and kept only plain, elderly attendants dressed in coarse silk nearby;

sentences.zh: 屏帳改用縑素；

translations.literal: Screens and curtains were replaced with plain white hemp;
translations.idiomatic: He replaced embroidered screens with plain hemp cloth;

sentences.zh: 故絕樂器之弦，不令拂去塵埃。

translations.literal: He deliberately broke the strings of musical instruments and did not allow the dust on them to be brushed away.
translations.idiomatic: He broke the strings of his instruments and left the dust on them undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 上見之，以為不好聲色，還宮，以語侍臣，意甚喜。

translations.literal: The emperor saw this, believed he did not care for music and women, returned to the palace, told his attendants, and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took this as proof Guang scorned pleasure and music; back at the palace he told his attendants, greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 侍臣皆稱慶，由是愛之特異諸子。

translations.literal: The attendants all offered congratulations; from this his favor became exceptional among the sons.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants offered congratulations; from that point his favor surpassed every other son.

sentences.zh: 上密令善相者來和遍視諸子，對曰：「晉王眉上雙骨隆起，貴不可言。

translations.literal: The emperor secretly ordered the skilled physiognomist Lai He to examine all the sons in turn; he replied: "Above Prince Jin's eyebrows the twin bones rise—nobility beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly had the physiognomist Lai He examine each son. Lai reported: "The twin bones above Prince Jin's brows rise high—fortune beyond telling.

sentences.zh: 」上又問上儀同三司韋鼎：「我諸兒誰得嗣位？

translations.literal: " The emperor also asked Senior Colonel of the Third Rank Wei Ding: "Among my sons, who will receive the succession?
translations.idiomatic: " He also asked Senior Colonel Wei Ding: "Which of my sons will inherit the throne?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「至尊、皇后所最愛者當與之，非臣敢預知也。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Whoever the Emperor and Empress love most should receive it—I dare not presume to know beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei answered: "Whoever Your Majesty and the empress love most—that is beyond my knowing.

sentences.zh: 」上笑曰：「卿不肯顯言邪！

translations.literal: " The emperor laughed: "You won't speak plainly, will you!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor laughed: "So you won't say it outright!

sentences.zh: 晉王廣美姿儀，性敏慧，沉深嚴重；

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Yang Guang had handsome bearing, a nature clever and quick, grave and dignified in depth;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin Yang Guang was handsome and quick-witted, grave and reserved by nature;

sentences.zh: 好學，善屬文；

translations.literal: He loved learning and was skilled at literary composition;
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and wrote well;

sentences.zh: 敬接朝士，禮極卑屈；

translations.literal: He received court gentlemen with respect, courtesy extremely humble and deferential;
translations.idiomatic: He treated court gentlemen with extreme deference;

sentences.zh: 由是聲名籍甚，冠於諸王。

translations.literal: From this his reputation spread greatly, surpassing all the princes.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation soared above every other prince.

sentences.zh: 廣為揚州總管，入朝，將還鎮，入宮辭後，伏地流涕，後亦泫然泣下。

translations.literal: Guang was military governor of Yangzhou; he entered court and, about to return to his command, entered the palace to bid the empress farewell; he prostrated himself and wept; the empress also shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: As Yangzhou military governor Guang came to court; before returning to his post he entered the palace to farewell the empress. He fell prostrate and wept; the empress wept too.

sentences.zh: 廣曰：「臣性識愚下，常守平生昆弟之意，不知何罪失愛東宮，恆蓄成怒，欲加屠陷。

translations.literal: Guang said: "My nature and understanding are dull and low; I have always upheld brotherly feeling as in ordinary days—I do not know what offense lost me the Eastern Palace's love; he constantly harbors settled wrath and wishes to slaughter and entrap me.
translations.idiomatic: Guang said: "I am slow-witted and have always kept brotherly affection—but somehow I've lost the Crown Prince's favor. He nurses a settled anger and wants my destruction.

sentences.zh: 每恐讒譖生於投杼，鴆毒遇於杯勺，是用勤憂積念，懼履危亡。

translations.literal: I constantly fear slander arising from the 'throwing-the-shuttle' doubt, poison meeting me in cup or ladle; therefore anxious care accumulates in my thoughts, and I fear treading toward ruin."
translations.idiomatic: I live in dread of slander—like the mother who doubted her son—and poison in every cup. Anxiety fills my days; I fear I am walking toward death."

sentences.zh: 」後忿然曰：「睍地伐漸不可耐，我為之娶元氏女，竟不以夫婦禮待之。

translations.literal: " The empress said angrily: "Min'diwo is gradually unbearable—I found him a Yuan girl as wife, yet he never treated her with husband-and-wife propriety.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress said furiously: "Min'diwo grows impossible—I chose a Yuan girl for his wife, and he never treated her as a wife should be treated.

sentences.zh: 專寵阿雲，使有如許豚犬。

translations.literal: He favors A-Yun alone, producing such pig-dog offspring.
translations.idiomatic: He dotes on A-Yun alone and fills the palace with worthless brats."

sentences.zh: 前新婦遇毒而夭，我亦不能窮治，何故復於汝發如此意！

translations.literal: The former bride met poison and died young—I could not thoroughly investigate that either; why do you now harbor such thoughts toward me!
translations.idiomatic: When the new bride died by poison I couldn't even pursue it fully—why must you turn such thoughts toward me now!

sentences.zh: 我在尚爾，我死後，當魚肉汝乎！

translations.literal: While I live it is still like this—after I die, will they carve you up like fish on a board!
translations.idiomatic: While I'm alive it comes to this—as when I'm gone, won't they cut you to pieces like fish on a board!

sentences.zh: 每思東宮竟無正嫡，至尊千秋萬歲之後，遣汝等兄弟向阿雲兒前再拜問訊，此是幾許苦痛邪！

translations.literal: Every time I think that the Eastern Palace ultimately has no legitimate principal consort—after the Emperor lives ten thousand years, to send you brothers to bow twice before A-Yun's son and inquire after him—how much bitterness is that!
translations.idiomatic: Every time I think the Eastern Palace has no legitimate heir—when the Emperor passes, you'll bow before A-Yun's brat—what humiliation is that!"

sentences.zh: 」廣又拜，嗚咽不能止，後亦悲不自勝。

translations.literal: " Guang bowed again, sobbing without cease; the empress also grieved beyond bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Guang bowed again, sobbing uncontrollably; the empress could not contain her grief.

sentences.zh: 自是後決意欲廢勇立廣矣。

translations.literal: From this the empress resolved to depose Yong and establish Guang.
translations.idiomatic: From that moment she resolved to depose Yong and make Guang heir.

sentences.zh: 廣與安州總管宇文述素善，欲述近己，奏為壽州刺史。

translations.literal: Guang had long been on good terms with Yuwen Shu, the regional commander of Anzhou; wishing to draw Shu closer to himself, he memorialized the throne to appoint him prefect of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guang had long been close to Yuwen Shu, the regional commander of Anzhou. Wanting Shu at his side, he memorialized the throne to have him appointed prefect of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 廣尤親任總管司馬張衡，衡為廣畫奪宗之策。

translations.literal: Guang especially trusted and relied on the regional commander's aide Zhang Heng; Heng devised for Guang a strategy to seize the succession.
translations.idiomatic: Guang placed particular trust in the commander's aide-de-camp, Zhang Heng, who drew up for him a plan to wrest away the heirship.

sentences.zh: 廣問計於述，述曰：「皇太子失愛已久，令德不聞於天下。

translations.literal: Guang sought Shu's counsel. Shu said: "The crown prince has long lost favor; his virtue and merit are unknown throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Guang asked Shu for advice. Shu said, "The crown prince has long fallen from grace, and his virtue is unheard of anywhere in the empire.

sentences.zh: 大王仁孝著稱，才能蓋世，數經將領，頻有大功；

translations.literal: Your Highness is renowned for benevolence and filial piety, your talent surpasses the age; you have repeatedly led armies and achieved many great victories;
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness is famed for benevolence and filial piety, and your abilities outshine the age. You have led armies time and again and won great victories one after another.

sentences.zh: 主上之與內宮，鹹所鍾愛，四海之望，實歸大王。

translations.literal: Both the emperor and the inner palace dote upon you; the hopes of all under Heaven truly belong to Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: Both His Majesty and the inner palace hold you dear, and the hopes of the whole realm truly rest with Your Highness.

sentences.zh: 然廢立者國家大事，處人父子骨肉之間，誠未易謀也。

translations.literal: Yet deposing and establishing an heir is a great matter of state, situated amid the bonds of father and son and flesh and blood—it is truly not easy to plot.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to depose one heir and install another is a grave affair of state, and it stands between a father and his own flesh and blood—truly no easy thing to scheme over.

sentences.zh: 然能移主上意者，唯楊素耳，素所與謀者唯其弟約。

translations.literal: Yet only Yang Su can shift the emperor's mind; the only one Su consults in plotting is his younger brother Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Still, the only man who can turn the emperor's mind is Yang Su, and the only man Su ever plots with is his younger brother Yue.

sentences.zh: 述雅知約，請朝京師，與約相見，共圖之。

translations.literal: Shu had long known Yue well. He requested leave to attend court in the capital, met with Yue, and together they plotted the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had known Yue well for years. He asked permission to go to the capital, met with Yue, and together they laid plans.

sentences.zh: 」廣大悅，多繼金寶，資述入關。

translations.literal: Guang was greatly pleased and supplied Shu with much gold and treasure to finance his entry into the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was delighted and gave Shu a great store of gold and jewels to fund his journey through the pass into the capital.

sentences.zh: 約時為大理少卿，素凡有所為，皆先籌於約而後行之。

translations.literal: At that time Yue was deputy director of the Court of Judicial Review; in everything Su undertook, he always deliberated first with Yue before acting.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was then deputy director of the Court of Judicial Review. In whatever Yang Su did, he always consulted Yue first and only then acted.

sentences.zh: 述請約，盛陳器玩，與之酣暢，因而共博，每陽不勝，所繼金寶盡輸之約。

translations.literal: Shu invited Yue, lavishly displaying curios and playthings; they drank freely together, then gambled, and each time Shu feigned defeat and lost all the gold and treasure he had brought to Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Shu invited Yue out, spread before him a lavish array of curios and fine objects, and they drank deep together. Then they gambled, and each time Shu pretended to lose, handing over every piece of gold and treasure he had brought.

sentences.zh: 約所得既多，稍以謝述。

translations.literal: Once Yue's gains were considerable, he began to thank Shu somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue had won a sizable sum, he began to thank Shu in earnest.

sentences.zh: 述因曰：「此晉王之賜，令述與公為歡樂耳。

translations.literal: Shu then said: "These were gifts from the Prince of Jin, meant only for Shu and you to enjoy together."
translations.idiomatic: Shu then said, "These were gifts from the Prince of Jin, sent so that you and I might enjoy ourselves together."

sentences.zh: 」約大驚曰：「何為爾？

translations.literal: Yue was greatly startled and said: "Why is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Yue was greatly alarmed and said, "What is the meaning of this?"

sentences.zh: 」述因通廣意，說之曰：「夫守正履道，固人臣之常致；

translations.literal: Shu then conveyed Guang's intent and persuaded him, saying: "To uphold rectitude and walk the proper path is indeed the ordinary duty of a minister;
translations.idiomatic: Shu then revealed Guang's intentions and pressed his case: "To hold to what is upright and walk the proper path is, to be sure, the usual duty of a minister.

sentences.zh: 反經合義，亦達者之令圖。

translations.literal: Yet to go against the letter of the law when it accords with righteousness is also the wise course of the discerning.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to bend the letter of the law when righteousness demands it is also the shrewd course of a man who sees clearly."

sentences.zh: 自古賢人君子，莫不與時消息以避禍患。

translations.literal: From antiquity, worthy men and gentlemen have all adjusted with the times to avoid calamity and peril.
translations.idiomatic: From ancient times, every worthy man and gentleman has shifted with the times to keep clear of disaster."

sentences.zh: 公之兄弟，功名蓋世，當途用事有年矣，朝臣為足下家所屈辱者，可勝數哉！

translations.literal: Your brothers' fame and achievement overshadow the age; they have held power at court for years—how countless are the court officials whom your family has humiliated!
translations.idiomatic: Your brothers' fame and deeds tower over the age. They have held power at court for years, and the officials your house has humbled are beyond counting!"

sentences.zh: 又，儲後以所欲不行，每切齒於執政；

translations.literal: Moreover, the heir apparent, thwarted in his desires, gnashes his teeth at those in power;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the heir apparent, denied what he wants, grinds his teeth at those who govern."

sentences.zh: 公雖自結於人主，而欲危公者固亦多矣！

translations.literal: Though you have cultivated ties with the sovereign yourself, those who wish you harm are indeed many!
translations.idiomatic: Though you have secured your own ties to the throne, there are many who would gladly see you ruined!"

sentences.zh: 主上一旦棄群臣，公亦何以取庇！

translations.literal: Once the emperor one day casts aside his ministers, how will you seek protection!
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor should one day cast his ministers aside, where will you turn for shelter?"

sentences.zh: 今皇太子失愛於皇后，主上素有廢黜之心，此公所知也。

translations.literal: Now the crown prince has lost the empress's favor, and the emperor has long harbored intent to depose him—you yourself know this.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince has already lost the empress's favor, and the emperor has long wished to remove him—you know this as well as anyone."

sentences.zh: 今若請立晉王，在賢兄之口耳。

translations.literal: If you now petition to install the Prince of Jin, it rests only on the word of your worthy brother.
translations.idiomatic: If you now petition to make the Prince of Jin heir, it would take no more than a word from your distinguished brother."

sentences.zh: 誠能因此時建大功，王必永銘骨髓，斯則去累卵之危，成太山之安也。

translations.literal: Truly, if you can at this juncture render a great service, the prince will engrave it upon his very marrow; thus you will escape danger as precarious as a pile of eggs and secure peace as firm as Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: If you can render a great service at this moment, the prince will remember it to his marrow. You will cast off danger piled like eggs one atop another and win security firm as Mount Tai."

sentences.zh: 」約然之，因以白素。

translations.literal: Yue agreed, and therefore reported this to Su.
translations.idiomatic: Yue agreed and reported the whole matter to Yang Su.

sentences.zh: 素聞之，大喜，撫掌曰：「吾之智思，殊不及此，賴汝啟予。

translations.literal: When Su heard of it, he was greatly pleased and clapped his hands, saying: "My wit and thought in no way reached this—I owe it to you for opening my eyes."
translations.idiomatic: When Su heard this, he was overjoyed. Clapping his hands, he said, "My own wit never reached so far—I owe this to you for opening my eyes."

sentences.zh: 」約知其計行，復謂素曰：「今皇后之言，上無不用，宜因機會早自結托，則長保榮祿，傳祚子孫。

translations.literal: Yue, knowing the plan would succeed, again said to Su: "The empress's words—the emperor never fails to heed them. You should seize this opportunity early to align yourself with her, and thus preserve honor and stipend for life and pass them to your descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, seeing that the plan would work, added, "The empress's words—the emperor never refuses them. You should seize this chance early and bind yourself to her. Then you will keep rank and emolument for life and pass them on to your children."

sentences.zh: 兄若遲疑，一旦有變，令太子用事，恐禍至無日矣！

translations.literal: Brother, if you hesitate, once things change and the crown prince comes to power, I fear disaster will arrive any day!
translations.idiomatic: Brother, if you delay, and the crown prince one day takes power, I fear ruin will come upon you almost at once!"

sentences.zh: 」素從之。

translations.literal: Su followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Su took his advice.

sentences.zh: 後數日，素入侍宴，微稱「晉王孝悌恭儉，有類至尊」。

translations.literal: Several days later, while attending the emperor at a banquet, Su subtly remarked that "the Prince of Jin is filial, fraternal, respectful, and frugal—much like Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: A few days later, while attending the emperor at a banquet, Yang Su casually remarked that the Prince of Jin was filial, brotherly, respectful, and frugal—in every way like the emperor himself.

sentences.zh: 用此揣後意。

translations.literal: With this he tested the empress's feelings.
translations.idiomatic: He used this to sound out the empress's mind.

sentences.zh: 後泣曰：「公言是也！

translations.literal: The empress wept and said: "Your words are true!
translations.idiomatic: The empress wept and said, "You speak the truth!

sentences.zh: 吾兒大孝愛，每聞至尊及我遣內使到，必迎於境首；

translations.literal: My son is deeply filial and loving. Whenever he hears that the emperor and I have sent palace emissaries, he always meets them at the border of his territory;
translations.idiomatic: That son of mine is deeply filial and loving. Whenever he hears that His Majesty or I have sent palace envoys, he always goes to the border of his domain to meet them.

sentences.zh: 言及違離，未嘗不泣。

translations.literal: When he speaks of separation, he never fails to weep.
translations.idiomatic: When he speaks of our separation, he never fails to weep."

sentences.zh: 又其新婦亦大可憐，我使婢去，常與之同寢共食。

translations.literal: Moreover his new bride is truly pitiable—I send maidservants to her, and she often sleeps and eats together with them.
translations.idiomatic: His new bride, too, is truly to be pitied. I send maids to her, and she often sleeps and eats together with them.

sentences.zh: 豈若睍地伐與阿雲對坐，終日酣宴，暱近小人，疑阻骨肉！

translations.literal: How unlike Modi and A-Yun sitting face to face, feasting all day long, clinging to petty men and sowing suspicion between kin!
translations.idiomatic: How unlike Modi and A-Yun, sitting face to face and feasting all day, dallying with petty men and sowing distrust among their own kin!

sentences.zh: 我所以益憐阿{麻女}者，常恐其潛殺之。

translations.literal: The reason I pity A-ma even more is that I constantly fear he will secretly have him killed.
translations.idiomatic: The reason I pity A-ma all the more is that I live in constant fear Modi will secretly have him killed."

sentences.zh: 」素既知後意，因盛言太子不才。

translations.literal: Once Su knew the empress's mind, he proceeded to speak at length of the crown prince's lack of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Once Su knew the empress's mind, he went on at length about the crown prince's lack of ability.

sentences.zh: 後遂遺素金，使贊上廢立。

translations.literal: The empress then sent Su gold and had him urge the emperor toward deposal and installation.
translations.idiomatic: The empress then sent Yang Su gold and had him press the emperor to depose the heir and install another.

sentences.zh: 勇頗知其謀，憂懼，計無所出，使新豐人王輔賢造諸厭勝；

translations.literal: Yong came to know something of the plot and was anxious and afraid; with no plan at hand, he had Wang Fujian of Xinfeng craft various counter-charms;
translations.idiomatic: Yong came to know something of the plot. Anxious and afraid, and with no plan to hand, he had Wang Fujian of Xinfeng prepare various apotropaic charms.

sentences.zh: 又於後園作庶人村，室屋卑陋，勇時於中寢息，布衣草褥，冀以當之。

translations.literal: He also built in the rear garden a "Village of Commoners" with low, shabby dwellings; Yong would sometimes sleep there on cloth bedding and straw mats, hoping this would avert fate.
translations.idiomatic: He also built in the rear garden a Commoners' Village of low, shabby houses. Yong would sometimes sleep there on coarse cloth and straw bedding, hoping by this to turn fate aside.

sentences.zh: 上知勇不自安，在仁壽宮，使楊素觀勇所為。

translations.literal: The emperor knew Yong was ill at ease; while at Renshou Palace, he sent Yang Su to observe Yong's actions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew Yong was ill at ease. While staying at Renshou Palace, he sent Yang Su to observe what Yong was doing.

sentences.zh: 素至東宮，偃息未入，勇束帶待之，素故久不進，以激怒勇；

translations.literal: When Su arrived at the Eastern Palace, he feigned rest and did not enter; Yong girded himself and waited, but Su deliberately stayed long without coming in to enrage Yong;
translations.idiomatic: When Su reached the Eastern Palace, he pretended to rest and would not go in. Yong girded himself and waited, but Su deliberately kept him waiting a long time to provoke him.

sentences.zh: 勇銜之，形於言色。

translations.literal: Yong harbored resentment, which showed in his words and countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Yong nursed the affront, and it showed in his words and face.

sentences.zh: 素還言：「勇怨望，恐有他變，願深防察！

translations.literal: On his return Su reported: "Yong is resentful and discontent; I fear there may be other changes—please guard against him with utmost vigilance!"
translations.idiomatic: On his return Su reported, "Yong is resentful and discontent. I fear he may attempt something else—Your Majesty should guard against him with the utmost care!"

sentences.zh: 」上聞素譖毀，甚疑之。

translations.literal: The emperor, having repeatedly heard Su's slander, grew deeply suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, having heard slander again and again, grew deeply suspicious.

sentences.zh: 後又遣人伺覘東宮，纖介事皆聞奏，因加誣飾以成其罪。

translations.literal: The empress also sent men to spy on the Eastern Palace; the slightest matters were all reported to the throne, and fabrications were added to complete his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The empress also sent men to spy on the Eastern Palace. The smallest matters were all reported to the throne, and false embellishments were piled on until his guilt was complete.

sentences.zh: 上遂疏忌勇，乃於玄武門達至德門量置候人，以伺動靜，皆隨事奏聞。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon grew distant and wary of Yong; he then stationed observers in proportion from the Xuanyang Gate to the Zhide Gate to watch comings and goings, all reporting as events occurred.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon grew cold and wary toward Yong. He posted lookouts in numbers all along the route from Xuanyang Gate to Zhide Gate to watch every movement, and each incident was reported as it happened.

sentences.zh: 又，東宮宿衛之人，侍官以上，名籍悉令屬諸衛府，有勇健者鹹屏去之。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Eastern Palace's resident guards—from chamberlains upward—all had their names transferred to the various guard offices, and the sturdiest were all removed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Eastern Palace's resident guards, from chamberlains upward, were all transferred on the rolls to the various guard offices, and the strongest among them were all removed.

sentences.zh: 出左衛率蘇孝慈為淅州刺史，勇愈不悅。

translations.literal: Zu Xiaoci, Left Guard Commander, was sent out as Prefect of Xizhou; Yong grew even more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Xiaoci, commander of the Left Guard, was sent out as prefect of Xizhou, and Yong grew even more unhappy.

sentences.zh: 太史令袁充言於上曰：「臣觀天文，皇太子當廢。

translations.literal: Astronomer Royal Yuan Chong said to the emperor: "Your servant observes the heavens—the crown prince is destined to be deposed."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chong, the director of the Astronomical Bureau, said to the emperor, "Your servant has read the heavens: the crown prince is fated to be deposed."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「玄象久見，群臣不敢言耳。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "These celestial signs have long been visible; the officials simply did not dare speak of them."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Those celestial signs have long been plain. The officials simply did not dare speak of them."

sentences.zh: 」充，君正之子也。

translations.literal: Chong was the son of Junzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was the son of Junzheng.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣又令督王府軍事姑臧段達私賂東宮幸臣姬威，令伺太子動靜，密告楊素；

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin, Guang, also had Duan Da of Guzang, military supervisor of the princely establishment, secretly bribe Ji Wei, a favored official of the Eastern Palace, to watch the crown prince's movements and secretly inform Yang Su;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin, Guang, also had Duan Da of Guzang, who oversaw the princely establishment's military affairs, secretly bribe Ji Wei, a favored minister of the Eastern Palace, to watch the crown prince's movements and report them in secret to Yang Su.

sentences.zh: 於是內外喧謗，過失日聞。

translations.literal: Thus slander swelled within and without, and offenses were heard of day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Slander then swelled inside and outside the palace, and fresh faults were reported day after day.

sentences.zh: 段達因脅姬威曰：「東宮過失，主上皆知之矣。

translations.literal: Duan Da then intimidated Ji Wei, saying: "The Eastern Palace's faults—the emperor already knows them all.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da then threatened Ji Wei, saying, "The crown prince's faults—the emperor already knows them all.

sentences.zh: 已奉密詔，定當廢立；

translations.literal: A secret edict has already been received; depossal and installation are certainly fixed;
translations.idiomatic: A secret edict has already been issued. His removal and replacement are settled.

sentences.zh: 君能告之，則大富貴！

translations.literal: If you can report them, great wealth and rank await!"
translations.idiomatic: If you will report them, great wealth and rank await you!"

sentences.zh: 」威許諾，即上書告之。

translations.literal: Ji Wei agreed and immediately submitted a written accusation.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Wei agreed and at once submitted a written denunciation.

sentences.zh: 秋，九月，壬子，上至自仁壽宮。

translations.literal: In autumn, the ninth month, on the day Renzi, the emperor arrived back from Renshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the ninth month, on the day Renzi, the emperor returned from Renshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 翌日，御大興殿，謂侍臣曰：「我新還京師，應開懷歡樂；

translations.literal: The next day, presiding in the Daxing Hall, he said to his attending ministers: "I have just returned to the capital and ought to open my heart in joy;
translations.idiomatic: The next day he took his seat in the Daxing Hall and said to the attending ministers, "I have just returned to the capital and ought to open my heart in joy.

sentences.zh: 不知何意翻邑然愁苦！

translations.literal: Yet for some reason I am instead gloomy and afflicted with sorrow!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet for some reason I am instead sunk in gloom and sorrow!"

sentences.zh: 」吏部尚書牛弘對曰：「臣等不稱職，故至尊憂勞。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Niu Hong replied: "Your servants are unworthy of their posts; hence Your Majesty's worry and toil."
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hong, minister of personnel, replied, "We have failed in our duties, and that is why Your Majesty is troubled and weary."

sentences.zh: 」上既數聞譖毀，疑朝臣悉知之，故於眾中發問，冀聞太子之過。

translations.literal: The emperor had repeatedly heard slander and suspected the court officials all knew of it; he therefore raised the question before the assembly, hoping to hear of the crown prince's faults.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had heard slander again and again and suspected that the whole court knew of it. He therefore raised the question in public, hoping someone would speak of the crown prince's faults.

sentences.zh: 弘對既失旨，上因作色，謂東宮官屬曰：「仁壽宮此去不遠，而令我每還京師，嚴備仗衛，如入敵國。

translations.literal: Hong's reply missed the mark; the emperor therefore changed expression and said to the Eastern Palace staff: "Renshou Palace is not far from here, yet each time I return to the capital I must rigorously arm my guards, as though entering enemy territory.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's answer missed the mark. The emperor's face darkened, and he said to the Eastern Palace officials, "Renshou Palace is not far away, yet every time I return to the capital I must arm my guards as if entering enemy country.

sentences.zh: 我為下利，不解衣臥。

translations.literal: When I need to relieve myself, I dare not undress to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: When I need to relieve myself, I dare not even undress to sleep.

sentences.zh: 昨夜欲近廁，故在後房恐有警急，還移就前殿，豈非爾輩欲壞我家國邪！

translations.literal: Last night, wishing to go to the privy, I feared an emergency in the rear chambers and moved to the front hall—is this not because you lot wish to ruin my house and state!"
translations.idiomatic: Last night, when I wanted to go to the privy, I feared something urgent in the rear chambers and moved to the front hall. Is this not because you mean to ruin my house and my realm?"

sentences.zh: 」於是執太子左庶子唐令則等數人付所司訊鞠；

translations.literal: Thereupon he seized several persons including the crown prince's Left Privy Counselor Tang Lingze and handed them over to the authorities for interrogation;
translations.idiomatic: He then seized several men, including the crown prince's left privy counselor Tang Lingze, and handed them over to the authorities for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 命楊素陳東宮事狀以告近臣。

translations.literal: He ordered Yang Su to set forth the Eastern Palace's circumstances and report them to the close ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yang Su to lay out the full account of the Eastern Palace and report it to the ministers closest to him.

sentences.zh: 素乃顯言之曰：「臣奉敕向京，令皇太子檢校劉居士餘黨。

translations.literal: Su then spoke openly, saying: "Your servant, by imperial order, came to the capital and directed the crown prince to investigate the remnant followers of Liu Jushi.
translations.idiomatic: Su then spoke openly: "Your servant, by imperial order, came to the capital and instructed the crown prince to investigate the remaining followers of Liu Jushi.

sentences.zh: 太子奉詔，作色奮厲，骨肉飛騰，語臣云：『居士黨盡伏法，遣我何處窮討！

translations.literal: The crown prince received the edict, changed color and grew fierce, his flesh and bone bristling with rage, and told me: "Liu Jushi's faction has all been executed—where am I sent to pursue them to the end!
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince received the edict, changed color, and flared up in fury until his whole body seemed to bristle. He told me, 'Liu Jushi's party has already been executed to the last man—where am I supposed to hunt them down!

sentences.zh: 爾作右僕射，委寄不輕，自檢校之，何關我事！

translations.literal: You serve as Right Vice Director—the trust placed in you is no light matter; investigate it yourself—what business is it of mine!"
translations.idiomatic: You are the right vice director. The trust placed in you is no small thing—investigate it yourself. What has that to do with me!'

sentences.zh: 』又云：『昔大事不遂，我先被誅，今作天子，竟乃令我不如諸弟，一事以上，不得自遂！

translations.literal: He also said: "When the great affair failed in the past, I was the first to be executed; now that I am son of Heaven, he still makes me inferior to my younger brothers—not in a single matter may I have my way!"
translations.idiomatic: He also said, 'When the great enterprise failed before, I was the first marked for death. Now that I am heir to the throne, he still makes me less than my younger brothers—not in one thing may I have my way!'

sentences.zh: 』因長歎回視云：『我大覺身妨。

translations.literal: Then he sighed long and, turning back, said: "I keenly feel myself to be in the way."
translations.idiomatic: Then he sighed deeply, looked back, and said, 'I feel more and more that I am in the way.'"

sentences.zh: 』」上曰：「此兒不堪承嗣久矣，皇后恆勸我廢之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This son has long been unfit to inherit; the empress has constantly urged me to depose him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "This son has long been unfit to succeed me. The empress has constantly urged me to remove him.

sentences.zh: 我以布衣時所生，地復居長，望其漸改，隱忍至今。

translations.literal: He was born when I was still a commoner, and again he ranks as eldest; I hoped he would gradually reform and have borne with it until now.
translations.idiomatic: He was born when I was still a commoner, and he is my eldest besides. I hoped he would mend by degrees, and so I have borne with him until now.

sentences.zh: 勇嘗指皇后侍兒謂人曰：『是皆我物。

translations.literal: Yong once pointed at the empress's maidservants and said to others: "These are all mine."
translations.idiomatic: Yong once pointed at the empress's maids and said to others, 'Those are all mine.'

sentences.zh: 』此言幾許異事！

translations.literal: What strange words are these!
translations.idiomatic: What strange words are these!

sentences.zh: 其婦初亡，我深疑其遇毒，嘗責之，勇即懟曰：『會殺元孝矩。

translations.literal: When his wife first died, I deeply suspected poison; I once rebuked him, and Yong immediately retorted: "I shall kill Yuan Xiaoju."
translations.idiomatic: When his wife first died, I strongly suspected poison. I once rebuked him, and Yong shot back, 'I will kill Yuan Xiaoju.'

sentences.zh: 』此欲害我而遷怒耳。

translations.literal: This was wishing to harm me and venting his anger elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to harm me and was merely venting his rage on someone else.

sentences.zh: 長寧初生，朕與皇后共抱養之，自懷彼此，連遣來索。

translations.literal: When Changning was first born, the empress and I together held and reared him, yet he felt estrangement from us and repeatedly sent to claim him.
translations.idiomatic: When Changning was first born, the empress and I together held and reared him, yet he kept us at a distance in his heart and sent again and again to take the child back.

sentences.zh: 且雲定興女，在外私合而生，想此由來，何必是其體胤！

translations.literal: Moreover it is said he is the daughter of Yun Dingxing, born from illicit union abroad—I think given such origins, why must he be my true flesh and blood!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, it is said she is the daughter of Yun Dingxing, born from a secret union abroad. Given such origins, why must she be my own flesh and blood!

sentences.zh: 昔晉太子取屠家女，其兒即好屠割。

translations.literal: In old times the Jin crown prince took a butcher's daughter; his son took pleasure in slaughtering and carving.
translations.idiomatic: In old times the Jin crown prince took a butcher's daughter, and his son delighted in slaughtering and carving flesh.

sentences.zh: 今倘非類，便亂宗祏。

translations.literal: If today he is not of the same kind, he would disorder the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: If today he is not of the same kind, he will throw the ancestral temple into disorder.

sentences.zh: 我雖德慚堯、舜，終不以萬姓付不肖子！

translations.literal: Though my virtue falls short of Yao and Shun, I will never entrust the myriad people to an unworthy son!
translations.idiomatic: Though my virtue falls short of Yao and Shun, I will never hand the myriad people over to an unworthy son!

sentences.zh: 我恆畏其加害，如防大敵；

translations.literal: I have constantly feared he would harm me, as though guarding against a great enemy;
translations.idiomatic: I have lived in constant fear that he would harm me, as if guarding against a great enemy.

sentences.zh: 今欲廢之以安天下！

translations.literal: Now I wish to depose him to secure all under Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Now I mean to remove him so that the realm may be secure!"

sentences.zh: 左衛大將軍五原公元旻諫曰：「廢立大事，詔旨若行，後悔無及。

translations.literal: Left Guard General Yuan Min, Duke of Wuyuan, remonstrated: "Depossal and installation are a great matter; if the edict is carried out, regret will come too late.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Min, Duke of Wuyuan and general of the Left Guard, remonstrated: "To depose one heir and install another is a grave matter. If the edict goes forth, regret will come too late.

sentences.zh: 讒言罔極，惟陛下察之。

translations.literal: Slander knows no limit—may Your Majesty examine it carefully."
translations.idiomatic: Slander knows no bounds. I beg Your Majesty to look into it with care."

sentences.zh: 上不應，命姬威悉陳太子罪惡。

translations.literal: The emperor did not respond; he ordered Ji Wei to set forth fully the crown prince's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made no reply. He ordered Ji Wei to set forth in full the crown prince's crimes.

sentences.zh: 威對曰：「太子由來與臣語，唯意在驕奢，且云：『若有諫者，正當斬之，不殺百許人，自然永息。

translations.literal: Ji Wei replied: "In all his speech with me the crown prince has cared only for arrogance and luxury, and he has said: "If anyone remonstrates, he should simply be beheaded; kill a hundred or so and naturally all will forever cease."
translations.idiomatic: Ji Wei replied, "In all his talk with me, the crown prince has cared only for arrogance and luxury. He has said, 'If anyone remonstrates, he should simply be beheaded. Kill a hundred or so, and naturally all will fall silent forever.'

sentences.zh: 』營起台殿，四時不輟。

translations.literal: He builds terraces and halls without pause through the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: He builds terraces and halls without cease through all four seasons.

sentences.zh: 前蘇孝慈解左衛率，太子奮髯揚肘曰：『大丈夫會當有一日，終不忘之，決當快意。

translations.literal: When Su Xiaoci was relieved of the Left Guard Command, the crown prince stroked his beard and flung his elbow, saying: "A real man will one day—not forgetting this—surely have his satisfaction."
translations.idiomatic: When Su Xiaoci was removed as commander of the Left Guard, the crown prince stroked his beard and threw back his elbow, saying, 'A real man will have his day. I will not forget this—I shall have my satisfaction yet.'

sentences.zh: 』又宮內所須，尚書多執法不與，輒怒曰：『僕射以下，吾會戮一二人，使知慢我之禍。

translations.literal: Moreover, for what the palace needed, the Secretariat often upheld the law and refused supply; he would angrily say: "From the vice directors down, I shall kill one or two to teach them the calamity of slighting me."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when the palace needed supplies, the Secretariat often upheld the law and refused them. He would rage and say, 'From the vice directors down, I will kill one or two so they learn the cost of slighting me.'

sentences.zh: 』每云：『至尊惡我多側庶，高緯、陳叔寶豈孽子乎！

translations.literal: He constantly said: "The emperor dislikes that I have many sons by concubines—were Gao Wei and Chen Shubao not sons by secondary wives!"
translations.idiomatic: He constantly said, 'His Majesty dislikes that I have many sons by concubines—were Gao Wei and Chen Shubao not sons by secondary wives!'

sentences.zh: 」嘗令師姥卜吉凶，語臣云：『至尊忌在十八年，此期促矣。

translations.literal: He once had a divining crone foretell good and ill, and told me: "The emperor's baleful star falls in the eighteenth year—that term draws near."
translations.idiomatic: He once had a divining crone read his fortune and told me, 'His Majesty's fatal year falls in the eighteenth year of the cycle—that day is close at hand.'"

sentences.zh: 』」上泫然曰：「誰非父母生，乃至於此！

translations.literal: The emperor said with tears: "Who is not born of parents—yet to come to this!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said through tears, "Who is not born of parents—yet to come to this!

sentences.zh: 朕近覽《齊書》，見高歡縱其兒子，不勝忿憤，安可傚尤邪！

translations.literal: Recently reading the Book of Qi, I saw how Gao Huan indulged his son and could not contain my indignation—how could we follow that bad example!"
translations.idiomatic: I have lately been reading the Book of Qi and saw how Gao Huan indulged his son. I could not contain my anger. How could we follow so foul an example!"

sentences.zh: 」於是禁勇及諸子，部分收其黨與。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Yong and his sons were confined, and some of his partisans were arrested.
translations.idiomatic: With that, Yang Yong and his sons were placed under confinement, and a portion of their associates were taken into custody.

sentences.zh: 楊素舞文巧詆，鍛煉以成其獄。

translations.literal: Yang Su twisted documents with artful slander and forged evidence to complete the case.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su manipulated the written record with cunning calumny and fabricated evidence until the prosecution was complete.

sentences.zh: 居數日，有司承素意，奏元旻常曲事於勇，情存附托，在仁壽宮，勇使所親裴弘以書與旻，題云：「勿令人見」。

translations.literal: After several days, the officials, following Su's intent, memorialized that Yuan Min had constantly curried favor with Yong and harbored allegiance to him; while at Renshou Palace, Yong had his close associate Pei Hong send a letter to Min, inscribed: "Let no one see this."
translations.idiomatic: A few days later, the judicial authorities, acting on Yang Su's wishes, reported that Yuan Min had long fawned upon Yong and kept himself ready to serve him. At Renshou Palace, Yong had his confidant Pei Hong deliver a letter to Min with the inscription: "Do not let anyone see this."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕在仁壽宮，有纖介事，東宮必知，疾於驛馬，怪之甚久，豈非此徒邪！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "When I am at Renshou Palace, even the slightest matter—the Eastern Palace always knows of it, faster than relay horses. I have wondered at this for a long time—is it not these people!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Whenever I am at Renshou Palace, even the smallest affair reaches the Eastern Palace sooner than a post horse. I have found that strange for a long time—surely it is these men!"

sentences.zh: 」遣武士執旻於仗。

translations.literal: " He sent warriors to seize Min at the guard post.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent armed guards to arrest Yuan Min at his post of duty.

sentences.zh: 右衛大將軍元冑時當下直，不去，因奏曰：「臣向不下直者，為防元旻耳。

translations.literal: Right Guard General Yuan Zhou was then due to go off duty but did not leave; he thereupon memorialized: "The reason I did not go off duty earlier was to guard against Yuan Min."
translations.idiomatic: Right Guard General Yuan Zhou was scheduled to leave his shift but stayed on, then submitted a memorial: "The reason I did not go off duty was to keep watch over Yuan Min."

sentences.zh: 」上以旻及裴弘付獄。

translations.literal: " The Emperor handed Min and Pei Hong over to prison.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had Min and Pei Hong thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 先是，勇見老枯槐，問：「此堪何用？

translations.literal: Earlier, Yong saw an old withered scholar tree and asked: "What could this be used for?"
translations.idiomatic: Previously, Yang Yong had noticed an old dead locust tree and asked, "What use could this serve?"

sentences.zh: 」或對曰：「古槐尤宜取火。

translations.literal: " Someone replied: "Ancient scholar trees are especially good for making fire."
translations.idiomatic: Someone answered, "Ancient locust wood is especially good for striking fire."

sentences.zh: 」時衛士皆佩火燧，勇命工造數千枚，欲以分賜左右；

translations.literal: " At the time the guards all carried fire-steels; Yong ordered craftsmen to make several thousand of them, intending to distribute them to his intimates;
translations.idiomatic: At that time the palace guards all carried fire-strikers. Yong ordered artisans to make several thousand of them, planning to give them out to his followers.

sentences.zh: 至是，獲於庫。

translations.literal: by this time they were seized from the storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: By now they were discovered in the storehouse.

sentences.zh: 又藥藏局貯艾數斛，索得之，大以為怪，以問姬威，威曰：「太子此意別有所在，至尊在仁壽宮，太子常飼馬千匹，云：『徑往守城門，自然餓死。

translations.literal: Also, the Pharmacy Bureau had stored several hu of mugwort; searching, they found it, and regarded it as very strange. They questioned Ji Wei, who said: "The Crown Prince's intent here lies elsewhere. When His Majesty is at Renshou Palace, the Crown Prince often keeps a thousand horses and says: 'Go straight to hold the city gates, and they will naturally starve to death.'"
translations.idiomatic: They also found several hu of mugwort stored in the Pharmaceutical Depot, and took this as highly suspicious. When they questioned Ji Wei, he said, "The Crown Prince's purpose in this is something else entirely. When His Majesty is at Renshou Palace, the Crown Prince keeps a thousand horses on hand and says, 'Ride straight to the city gates and hold them—they will starve of their own accord.'"

sentences.zh: 』」素以威言詰勇，勇不服，曰：「竊聞公家馬數萬匹，勇忝備太子，馬千匹，乃是反乎！

translations.literal: " Yang Su used Wei's words to confront Yong; Yong would not accept it and said: "I have heard that the government keeps tens of thousands of horses; I, Yong, humbly hold the position of Crown Prince—a thousand horses, and that is treason!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su pressed Yong with Wei's testimony. Yong refused to accept the charge and said, "I have heard that the state keeps tens of thousands of horses. I, Yong, happen to be Crown Prince—are a thousand horses treason?"

sentences.zh: 」素又發東宮服玩，似加琱飾者，悉陳之於庭，以示文武群官，為太子之罪。

translations.literal: " Yang Su also brought out the Eastern Palace's garments and ornaments—those that seemed lavishly carved and decorated—arrayed them all in the courtyard, and displayed them before civil and military officials as evidence of the Crown Prince's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su also had the Eastern Palace's robes and curios—anything that looked extravagantly ornamented—brought out and laid in the courtyard to show the assembled civil and military officials as proof of the Crown Prince's offenses.

sentences.zh: 上及皇后迭遣使責問勇，勇不服。

translations.literal: The Emperor and Empress sent messengers in succession to rebuke and question Yong; Yong would not accept the charges.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor and Empress dispatched envoys one after another to reproach and interrogate Yong, but he would not concede guilt.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙丑，上使人召勇，勇見使者，驚曰：「得無殺我邪？

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on yichou, the Emperor sent someone to summon Yong. When Yong saw the messenger, he said in alarm: "Surely they are not going to kill me?"
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on the day yichou, the Emperor sent for Yong. When Yong saw the messenger, he cried out in fear, "They aren't going to kill me, are they?"

sentences.zh: 」上戎服陳兵，御武德殿，集百官立於東面，諸親立於西面，引勇及諸子列於殿庭，命內史侍郎薛道衡宣詔，廢勇及其男、女為王、公主者，並為庶人。

translations.literal: " The Emperor, in military dress with troops arrayed, took his seat at Wude Hall, gathered the officials standing on the east, kinsmen on the west, brought forth Yong and his sons lined up in the court of the hall, and ordered Secretariat Vice Minister Xue Daoheng to read the edict deposing Yong and all his sons who were kings and daughters who were princesses, reducing them all to commoners.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor appeared in martial garb with troops drawn up, presided in Wude Hall, assembled the officials on the east and the imperial kinsmen on the west, and had Yong and his sons brought forward and lined up in the courtyard. He ordered Secretariat Vice Minister Xue Daoheng to proclaim the edict deposing Yong and reducing to commoner status all his sons who had been enfeoffed as kings and all his daughters who had been made princesses.

sentences.zh: 勇再拜言曰：「臣當伏屍都市，為將來鑒戒；

translations.literal: Yong bowed twice and said: "Your subject ought to lie dead in the marketplace as a warning for the future;"
translations.idiomatic: Yong bowed twice and said, "Your subject deserves to lie dead in the public square as a warning to those who come after."

sentences.zh: 幸蒙哀憐，得全性命！

translations.literal: yet thankfully, through Your merciful pity, I preserve my life!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet by your gracious mercy I am allowed to keep my life!"

sentences.zh: 」言畢，泣下流襟，既而舞蹈而去，左右莫不閔默。

translations.literal: " When he finished speaking, tears streamed down his collar; then he bowed in the dance rite and withdrew, and none beside him failed to grieve in silence.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished, tears soaked the front of his robe. He then performed the parting obeisance and withdrew, and everyone present grieved in silence.

sentences.zh: 長寧王儼上表乞宿衛，辭情哀切；

translations.literal: Prince of Changning, Yan, submitted a memorial begging to serve on night guard, his words pitifully earnest;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Changning, Yang Yan, submitted a memorial begging to remain on night watch; his language was heartbreakingly sincere.

sentences.zh: 上覽之閔然。

translations.literal: the Emperor read it and was moved to sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor read it, he was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 楊素進曰：「伏望聖心同於螫手，不宜復留意。

translations.literal: Yang Su stepped forward and said: "I humbly hope Your Sacred Heart will be like one who has been stung on the hand—You should not dwell on this further."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su stepped forward and said, "I beg Your Majesty to treat this as one treats a hand that has been stung—do not let your heart linger on it any longer."

sentences.zh: 己巳，詔：「元旻、唐令則及太子家令鄒文騰、左衛率司馬夏侯福、典膳監元淹、前吏部侍郎蕭子寶、前主璽下士何竦並處斬，妻妾子孫皆沒官。

translations.literal: On jisi, an edict: "Yuan Min, Tang Lingze, the Crown Prince's Household Steward Zou Wenteng, Left Guard Commandant's Major Xia Houfu, Provisioners Commissioner Yuan Yan, former Ministry of Personnel Vice Minister Xiao Zibao, and former Chief Seal Lower Gentleman He Song are all to be executed; their wives, concubines, and descendants are all to be enslaved as government property."
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, an edict declared: "Yuan Min, Tang Lingze, the Crown Prince's household steward Zou Wenteng, Left Guard Commandant's major Xia Houfu, Provisioners Commissioner Yuan Yan, former Vice Minister of Personnel Xiao Zibao, and former Chief Seal Attendant He Song shall all be executed, and their wives, concubines, and descendants shall be confiscated as government slaves."

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍榆林閻毘、東郡公崔君綽、游騎尉沈福寶、瀛州術士章仇太翼，特免死，各杖一百，身及妻子、資財、田宅皆沒官。

translations.literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry Yan Pi of Yulin, Duke of Dongjun Cui Junchuo, Cavalry Commandant Shen Fubao, and Yingzhou occultist Zhangqiu Taiyi are specially spared death, each to receive a hundred blows with the staff; their persons, wives, children, property, fields, and houses are all forfeited to the government.
translations.idiomatic: General of Chariots and Cavalry Yan Pi of Yulin, Duke of Dongjun Cui Junchuo, Cavalry Commandant Shen Fubao, and the Yingzhou diviner Zhangqiu Taiyi were specially spared execution and instead each received a hundred strokes of the rod; they themselves, their wives and children, their property, fields, and houses were all confiscated.

sentences.zh: 副作大匠高龍叉、率更令晉文建、通直散騎侍郎元衡皆處盡。

translations.literal: Assistant Master Craftsman Gao Longcha, Director of the Water Clock Jin Wenjian, and Attendant Cavalier Regular Gentleman Yuan Heng are all to be executed to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Master Craftsman Gao Longcha, Director of the Water Clock Jin Wenjian, and Attendant Cavalier Regular Gentleman Yuan Heng were all executed along with their families.

sentences.zh: 」於是集群官於廣陽門外，宣詔戮之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the officials were assembled outside the Guangyang Gate, the edict was proclaimed, and they were executed.
translations.idiomatic: The officials were then gathered outside Guangyang Gate, the edict was read aloud, and the condemned were put to death.

sentences.zh: 乃移勇於內史省，給五品料食。

translations.literal: Yong was then moved to the Secretariat Directorate and granted fifth-rank provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was then transferred to the Secretariat Directorate and given provisions befitting a fifth-rank official.

sentences.zh: 賜楊素物三千段，元冑、楊約並千段，賞鞫勇之功也。

translations.literal: Yang Su was granted three thousand bolts of goods, Yuan Zhou and Yang Yue each a thousand bolts, in reward for their work in investigating Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su was rewarded with three thousand bolts of goods, and Yuan Zhou and Yang Yue each with a thousand bolts, in recognition of their service in prosecuting Yong.

sentences.zh: 文林郎楊孝政上書諫曰：「皇太子為小人所誤，宜加訓誨，不宜廢黜。

translations.literal: Scholar-librarian Yang Xiaozheng submitted a memorial remonstrating: "The Crown Prince has been misled by petty men; he should be given further instruction and admonition, not deposed."
translations.idiomatic: Palace Scholar Yang Xiaozheng submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "The Crown Prince has been led astray by petty men. He ought to be corrected and instructed, not deposed."

sentences.zh: 」上怒，撻其胸。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was enraged and struck him on the chest.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flew into a rage and beat him on the chest.

sentences.zh: 初，雲昭訓父定興，出入東宮無節，數進奇服異器以求悅媚；

translations.literal: Earlier, Yun Zhaoxun's father Dingxing came and went from the Eastern Palace without restraint, repeatedly presenting strange garments and unusual objects to win favor;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yun Zhaoxun's father Yang Dingxing had come and gone from the Eastern Palace without restraint, repeatedly offering outlandish clothes and curious objects to please and flatter the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 左庶子裴屢諫，勇不聽。

translations.literal: Left Counselor Pei Zheng repeatedly remonstrated, but Yong would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Left Counselor Pei Zheng remonstrated again and again, but Yong would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 政謂定興曰：「公所為不合法度。

translations.literal: Zheng said to Dingxing: "What you are doing does not accord with law and propriety."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zheng told Dingxing, "Your conduct does not conform to proper standards."

sentences.zh: 又，元妃暴薨，道路籍籍，此於太子，非令名也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Primary Consort died suddenly, and rumors filled the roads—this is not a good name for the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Crown Princess died suddenly, and gossip ran rife through the streets—this does the Crown Prince no credit.

sentences.zh: 公宜自引退，不然，將及禍。

translations.literal: You ought to withdraw on your own; otherwise disaster will overtake you."
translations.idiomatic: You should remove yourself before it is too late; otherwise calamity will find you."

sentences.zh: 」定興以告勇，勇益疏政，由是出為襄州總管。

translations.literal: " Dingxing told Yong, and Yong grew all the more distant from Zheng; for this reason Zheng was sent out as Regional Commander of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxing reported this to Yong, and Yong grew still colder toward Pei Zheng, who was eventually sent out to serve as regional commander of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 唐令則為勇所暱狎，每令以弦歌教內人，右庶子劉行本責之曰：「庶子當輔太子以正道，何有取媚於房帷之間哉！

translations.literal: Tang Lingze was intimate with Yong; he was often made to teach the inner women with lute and song. Right Counselor Liu Xingben rebuked him: "A counselor ought to assist the Crown Prince on the righteous path—what business is there in currying favor within the bedchamber!"
translations.idiomatic: Tang Lingze was on familiar terms with Yong and was often ordered to instruct the palace women in music and song. Right Counselor Liu Xingben rebuked him: "A counselor's duty is to guide the Crown Prince along the right path—what place is there for winning favor in the inner quarters!"

sentences.zh: 」令則甚慚而不能改。

translations.literal: " Lingze was deeply ashamed but could not change.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Lingze was deeply ashamed, but he could not mend his ways.

sentences.zh: 時沛國劉臻、平原明克讓、魏郡陸爽，並以文學為勇所親；

translations.literal: At the time Liu Zhen of Pei, Ming Kerang of Pingyuan, and Lu Shuang of Weijun were all favored by Yong for their literary learning;
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Zhen of Pei, Ming Kerang of Pingyuan, and Lu Shuang of Weijun were all close to Yong for their literary accomplishments.

sentences.zh: 行本怒其不能調護，每謂三人曰：「卿等正解讀書耳！

translations.literal: Xingben, angered that they could not guide and protect him, would often tell the three: "You people only know how to read books!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xingben, angry that they failed to guide and protect the Crown Prince, would often say to the three of them, "All you know how to do is read books!"

sentences.zh: 」夏侯福嘗於閣內與勇戲，福大笑，聲聞於外。

translations.literal: " Xia Houfu once played with Yong inside the pavilion; Fu laughed loudly, and the sound was heard outside.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Houfu once amused himself with Yong inside the pavilion; he laughed so loudly that the sound carried outside.

sentences.zh: 行本聞之，待其出，數之曰：「殿下寬容，賜汝顏色。

translations.literal: Xingben heard it and, waiting until he came out, rebuked him: "His Highness, in his magnanimity, bestows his favor upon you."
translations.idiomatic: When Xingben heard this, he waited until Xia Houfu came out and scolded him: "His Highness, in his forbearance, has shown you favor."

sentences.zh: 汝何物小人，敢為褻慢！

translations.literal: You worthless little man—how dare you behave with such disrespect!"
translations.idiomatic: What sort of base creature are you, to behave with such disrespect!"

sentences.zh: 」因付執法者治之。

translations.literal: " He then handed him over to the law officers for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He then handed him over to the disciplinary officers for punishment.

sentences.zh: 數日，勇為福致請，乃釋之。

translations.literal: Several days later, Yong interceded on Fu's behalf, and he was released.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Yong pleaded for Xia Houfu, and he was released.

sentences.zh: 勇嘗得良馬，欲令行本乘而觀之，行本正色曰：「至尊置臣於庶子，欲令輔導殿下，非為殿下作弄臣也。
