translations.literal: Yong once obtained a fine horse and wanted Xingben to mount it so he could watch; Xingben, with stern countenance, said: "His Majesty placed me as counselor precisely to guide and instruct Your Highness—not to serve as Your Highness's plaything."
translations.idiomatic: Yong once acquired a fine horse and wanted Xingben to ride it while he looked on. Xingben's face hardened as he said, "His Majesty appointed me counselor in order to guide and instruct Your Highness—not to become Your Highness's court jester."

sentences.zh: 」勇慚而止。

translations.literal: " Yong, ashamed, desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Yong dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 及勇敗，二人已卒，上歎曰：「向使裴政、劉行本在，勇不至此。

translations.literal: When Yong fell, both men had already died; the Emperor sighed and said: "If only Pei Zheng and Liu Xingben had been there, Yong would not have come to this."
translations.idiomatic: By the time Yong fell from power, both men were already dead. The Emperor sighed and said, "If only Pei Zheng and Liu Xingben had still been there, Yong would never have come to this pass."

sentences.zh: 勇嘗宴宮臣，唐令則自彈琵琶，歌《嫵媚娘》。

translations.literal: Yong once feasted his palace officers; Tang Lingze himself played the pipa and sang "Wumei Niang."
translations.idiomatic: Yong once entertained his palace staff. Tang Lingze played the pipa himself and sang "The Charming Maid."

sentences.zh: 洗馬李綱起白勇曰：「令則身為宮卿，職當調護；

translations.literal: Mentor Li Gang rose and addressed Yong: "Lingze holds the rank of a palace minister; his duty is to guide and protect;"
translations.idiomatic: Mentor Li Gang rose and addressed Yong: "Tang Lingze is a palace minister. His duty is to guide and protect you."

sentences.zh: 乃於廣座自比倡優，進淫聲，穢視聽。

translations.literal: yet here, before this broad assembly, he compares himself to musicians and actors, offering licentious songs that foul the eyes and ears.
translations.idiomatic: Yet here, before this whole gathering, he puts himself on a level with entertainers and actors, performing lewd songs that defile sight and hearing.

sentences.zh: 事若上聞，令則罪在不測，豈不為殿下之累邪！

translations.literal: If this reaches the Emperor's ears, Lingze's guilt would be beyond reckoning—would it not also be a liability to Your Highness!
translations.idiomatic: If word of this reaches the Emperor, Tang Lingze's offense will be beyond measure—and will it not also bring ruin upon Your Highness!

sentences.zh: 臣請速治其罪！

translations.literal: Your subject requests that his offense be punished at once!"
translations.idiomatic: I beg that he be punished immediately!"

sentences.zh: 」勇曰：「我欲為樂耳，君勿多事！

translations.literal: " Yong said: "I only wanted some amusement—do not meddle!"
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "I only wanted a little amusement—stay out of it!"

sentences.zh: 」綱遂趨出。

translations.literal: " Gang thereupon hurried out.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang then rushed out.

sentences.zh: 及勇廢，上召東宮官屬切責之，皆惶懼無敢對者。

translations.literal: When Yong was deposed, the Emperor summoned the Eastern Palace staff and sharply rebuked them; all were fearful and none dared reply.
translations.idiomatic: After Yong was deposed, the Emperor summoned the Eastern Palace officials and rebuked them severely. All were terrified, and no one dared answer.

sentences.zh: 綱獨曰：「廢立大事，今文武大臣皆知其不可，而莫肯發言，臣何敢畏死，不一為陛下別白言之乎！

translations.literal: Gang alone said: "Deposition and installation are a great matter. Today civil and military ministers all know this should not be done, yet none will speak. How dare I, fearing death, fail to set it forth clearly once for Your Majesty!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang alone spoke up: "Deposing and installing an heir is a momentous affair. Every civil and military minister in court knows this was wrong, yet none would speak. How could I, for fear of death, fail to set the truth plainly before Your Majesty even once!"

sentences.zh: 太子性本中人，可與為善，可與為惡。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince's nature is middling—he can be led toward good or toward evil.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince's character is neither good nor bad by nature; he can be led toward virtue or toward vice.

sentences.zh: 向使陛下擇正人輔之，足以嗣守鴻基。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty had chosen upright men to assist him, he would have been sufficient to inherit and guard the great foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Had Your Majesty chosen upright men to assist him, he would have been fully capable of inheriting and preserving the imperial foundation.

sentences.zh: 今乃以唐令則為左庶子，鄒文騰為家令，二人唯知以弦歌鷹犬娛悅太子，安得不至於是邪！

translations.literal: Yet now Tang Lingze was made Left Counselor and Zou Wenteng Household Steward—the two knew only to amuse the Crown Prince with lute, song, hawks, and hounds; how could it not have come to this!
translations.idiomatic: Instead Tang Lingze was made Left Counselor and Zou Wenteng household steward—men who knew only how to divert the Crown Prince with music, hunting hawks, and dogs. How could matters not have ended this way!

sentences.zh: 此乃陛下之過，非太子之罪也。

translations.literal: This is Your Majesty's fault, not the Crown Prince's crime."
translations.idiomatic: This is Your Majesty's failing, not the Crown Prince's crime."

sentences.zh: 」因伏地流涕嗚咽。

translations.literal: " He then prostrated himself, weeping and sobbing.
translations.idiomatic: He then prostrated himself, weeping and choking with grief.

sentences.zh: 上慘然良久曰：「李綱責我，非為無理，然徒知其一，未知其二。

translations.literal: The Emperor, grim-faced for a long while, said: "Li Gang reproaches me—not without reason—yet he knows only the one part and not the other."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor looked grim for a long moment and said, "Li Gang's rebuke is not without reason, but he sees only one side and not the other."

sentences.zh: 我擇汝為宮臣，而勇不親任，雖更得正人，何益哉！

translations.literal: I chose you as a palace officer, yet Yong would not trust you intimately; even if we had gotten better men, what good would it have done!"
translations.idiomatic: I chose you as a palace officer, yet Yong would not place his trust in you. Even if we had found better men, what good would it have done!"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣所以不被親任者，良由奸臣在側故也。

translations.literal: " He replied: "The reason I was not trusted is precisely because villainous ministers were at his side."
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang replied, "The reason I was not trusted was simply that wicked ministers stood at his side."

sentences.zh: 陛下但斬令則、文騰，更選賢才以輔太子，安知臣之終見疏棄也！

translations.literal: If Your Majesty would only execute Lingze and Wenteng and choose worthy talents to assist the Crown Prince, how can you know that I would forever remain estranged!"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would execute Tang Lingze and Zou Wenteng and choose worthy men to assist the Crown Prince, how can you be sure I would remain estranged forever!"

sentences.zh: 自古廢立塚嫡，鮮不傾危，願陛下深留聖思，無貽後悔。

translations.literal: From antiquity, deposing and installing the heir of the main line has rarely failed to bring downfall and peril; I beg Your Majesty to ponder deeply and leave no cause for regret."
translations.idiomatic: Since ancient times, deposing the legitimate heir has rarely failed to bring disaster. I beg Your Majesty to weigh this carefully and leave no room for later regret."

sentences.zh: 」上不悅，罷朝，左右皆為之股慄。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was displeased and adjourned court; all those beside him trembled in their thighs.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was displeased and dismissed court. Everyone around him trembled with fear.

sentences.zh: 會尚書右丞缺，有司請人，上指綱曰：「此佳右丞也！

translations.literal: As it happened the Right Assistant Minister of the Secretariat was vacant; the officials requested an appointment, and the Emperor pointed at Gang and said: "This man is an excellent Right Assistant Minister!"
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the post of Right Assistant Minister of the Secretariat was vacant. When the officials asked whom to appoint, the Emperor pointed at Li Gang and said, "He will make an excellent Right Assistant Minister!"

sentences.zh: 」即用之。

translations.literal: " He was immediately appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang was appointed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 太平公史萬歲還自大斤山，楊素害其功，言於上曰：「突厥本降，初不為寇，來塞上畜牧耳。

translations.literal: Duke of Taiping Shi Wansui returned from Great Jin Mountain; Yang Su, jealous of his achievement, said to the Emperor: "The Turks had already surrendered; they were not raiding at first—they merely came to graze their herds on the frontier."
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Taiping Shi Wansui returned from Mount Dajin. Yang Su, resentful of his victory, told the Emperor, "The Turks had already submitted. They were not raiding at all—they had merely come to graze their herds along the frontier."

sentences.zh: 」遂寢之。

translations.literal: " The matter was therefore shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was accordingly set aside.

sentences.zh: 萬歲數抗表陳狀，上未之悟。

translations.literal: Wansui repeatedly submitted memorials stating the facts, but the Emperor did not grasp it.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wansui submitted memorial after memorial setting out the facts, but the Emperor failed to understand.

sentences.zh: 上廢太子，方窮東宮黨與。

translations.literal: When the Emperor deposed the Crown Prince, he was then pursuing the Eastern Palace factions.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor deposed the Crown Prince, he was at the same time hunting down the Eastern Palace faction.

sentences.zh: 上問萬歲所在，萬歲實在朝堂，楊素曰：「萬歲謁東宮矣！

translations.literal: The Emperor asked where Wansui was; Wansui was in fact at the court hall, but Yang Su said: "Wansui has gone to visit the Eastern Palace!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked where Shi Wansui was. Wansui was in fact at court, but Yang Su said, "Wansui has gone to call on the Eastern Palace!"

sentences.zh: 」以激怒上。

translations.literal: " to provoke the Emperor's anger.
translations.idiomatic: He said this to inflame the Emperor's wrath.

sentences.zh: 上謂為信然，令召萬歲。

translations.literal: The Emperor believed it was true and ordered Wansui summoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took this for truth and ordered Shi Wansui summoned.

sentences.zh: 時所將士在朝堂稱冤者數百人，萬歲謂之曰：「吾今日為汝極言於上，事當決矣。

translations.literal: At the time several hundred of the troops he had led were at the court hall claiming injustice; Wansui told them: "Today I will speak out to the utmost for you before the Emperor—the matter should be settled."
translations.idiomatic: At that moment several hundred of the soldiers he had commanded were in the hall protesting their mistreatment. Wansui told them, "Today I will plead your case to the utmost before the Emperor. This should be decided once and for all."

sentences.zh: 」既見上，言「將士有功，為朝廷所抑！

translations.literal: " When he saw the Emperor, he said, "The troops have merit, yet they are being suppressed by the court!"
translations.idiomatic: When he appeared before the Emperor, he declared, "These soldiers have earned merit, yet the court is suppressing them!"

sentences.zh: 」詞氣憤厲。

translations.literal: " His tone was fierce and indignant.
translations.idiomatic: His words were fierce and indignant.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，令左右Ξ殺之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly enraged and ordered those beside him to beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious and ordered his attendants to beat Shi Wansui to death on the spot.

sentences.zh: 既而追之，不及，因下詔陳其罪狀，天下共冤惜之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he sent pursuers, but they could not overtake them; he then issued an edict setting forth Wansui's crimes, and all under Heaven alike grieved at the injustice.
translations.idiomatic: He soon sent men to recall the order, but it was too late. An edict was then issued listing Wansui's crimes, and people throughout the empire mourned the injustice.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊子，立晉王廣為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on wuzi, Prince of Jin Guang was installed as Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day wuzi, Prince Jin Yang Guang was installed as Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 天下地震，太子請降章服，宮官不稱臣。

translations.literal: There was an earthquake throughout the realm; the Crown Prince requested to lower his rank insignia and robes, and the palace officers did not address themselves as "your subject."
translations.idiomatic: An earthquake shook the empire. The new Crown Prince asked to reduce his ceremonial insignia and robes, and the palace officials ceased addressing themselves as subjects.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊午，詔從之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on wuwu, an edict granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day wuwu, an edict approved his request.

sentences.zh: 以宇文述為左衛率。

translations.literal: Yuwen Shu was appointed Left Guard Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shu was appointed Left Guard Commandant.

sentences.zh: 始，太子之謀奪宗也，洪州總管郭衍預焉，由是征衍為左監門率。

translations.literal: At the outset, when the Crown Prince plotted to seize the succession, Hongzhou Regional Commander Guo Yan took part; for this reason Yan was summoned and made Left Gate Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: From the beginning, when the Crown Prince plotted to seize the succession, Hongzhou regional commander Guo Yan had taken part; for this he was summoned to court and appointed Left Gate Commandant.

sentences.zh: 帝囚故太子勇於東宮，付太子廣掌之。

translations.literal: The Emperor imprisoned the former Crown Prince Yong in the Eastern Palace and entrusted him to Crown Prince Guang to manage.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor imprisoned the former Crown Prince Yong in the Eastern Palace and placed him under Crown Prince Guang's supervision.

sentences.zh: 勇自以廢非其罪，頻請見上申冤，而廣遏之不得聞。

translations.literal: Yong himself believed his deposition was not his crime; he repeatedly requested an audience with the Emperor to proclaim his innocence, but Guang blocked it so the Emperor could not hear.
translations.idiomatic: Yong believed he had been deposed without cause and repeatedly asked to see the Emperor to plead his innocence, but Guang prevented it and the Emperor never heard him.

sentences.zh: 勇於是升樹大叫，聲聞帝所，冀得引見。

translations.literal: Yong therefore climbed a tree and shouted loudly, his voice reaching the Emperor's quarters, hoping to gain an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Yong then climbed a tree and shouted at the top of his voice until the sound reached the Emperor's residence, hoping to be summoned.

sentences.zh: 楊素因言勇情志昏亂，為癲鬼所著，不可復收。

translations.literal: Yang Su thereupon said Yong's mind and emotions were disordered, that he was possessed by a mad demon, and could not be taken back.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su then said that Yong's mind was deranged, that he was possessed by a mad demon, and could not be reclaimed.

sentences.zh: 帝以為然，卒不得見。

translations.literal: The Emperor believed it was so, and in the end Yong was never granted an audience.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted this explanation, and Yong was never allowed to see him.

sentences.zh: 初，帝之克陳也，天下皆以為將太平，監察御史房彥謙私謂所親曰：「主上忌刻而苛酷，太子卑弱，諸王擅權，天下雖安，方憂危亂。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor conquered Chen, all under Heaven believed peace was near; Supervising Censor Fang Yanqian said privately to those close to him: "Our lord is jealous, harsh, and cruel; the Crown Prince is weak; the princes wield power on their own. Though the realm is at peace, I already fear turmoil."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Emperor conquered Chen, the empire believed universal peace was at hand. Supervising Censor Fang Yanqian said privately to those close to him, "The sovereign is jealous, harsh, and cruel; the Crown Prince is weak; the princes each hold power in their own right. Though the realm appears secure, I already foresee disorder."

sentences.zh: 」其子玄齡亦密言於彥謙曰：「主上本無功德，以詐取天下，諸子皆驕奢不仁，必自相誅夷，今雖承平，其亡可翹足待。

translations.literal: " His son Xuanling also spoke secretly to Yanqian: "Our lord originally had no merit—he seized the realm by deceit. His sons are all arrogant, extravagant, and unkind; they will surely destroy one another. Though we now enjoy peace, its fall can be awaited with toes crossed."
translations.idiomatic: His son Fang Xuanling also spoke privately to Yanqian, "The sovereign had no real merit to begin with; he won the realm through deception. His sons are all arrogant, extravagant, and cruel. They will surely destroy one another. Though the age looks peaceful now, its collapse can be awaited with folded legs."

sentences.zh: 」彥謙，法壽之玄孫也。

translations.literal: " Yanqian was the great-great-grandson of Fang Fashou.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Yanqian was the great-great-grandson of Fang Fashou.

sentences.zh: 玄齡與杜果之兄孫如晦皆預選，吏部侍郎高孝基名知人，見玄齡，歎曰：「僕閱人多矣，未見如此郎者，異日必為偉器，恨不見其大成耳！

translations.literal: Xuanling and Du Ruhui, grandson of Du Guo's elder brother, were both selected in advance; Vice Minister of Personnel Gao Xiaoji, famed for recognizing talent, saw Xuanling and exclaimed: "I have read men for many years and never seen a young man like this; someday he will surely become a great vessel—I regret only that I shall not see him reach his full maturity!"
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui, grandson of Du Guo's elder brother, were both selected for office. Gao Xiaoji, Vice Minister of Personnel and a renowned judge of men, saw Xuanling and exclaimed, "I have observed men all my life and never seen a young man like this one. Someday he will become a pillar of the state—I only regret that I shall not live to see him reach his full stature!"

sentences.zh: 」見如晦，謂曰：「君有應變之才，必任棟樑之重。

translations.literal: " Seeing Ruhui, he said: "You possess the talent to adapt to change; you will surely bear the weight of a pillar and beam."
translations.idiomatic: When he saw Du Ruhui, he said, "You have the talent to meet changing circumstances. You will surely bear the weight of a great pillar."

sentences.zh: 」俱以子孫托之。

translations.literal: " To both of them he entrusted his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: To both of them he entrusted his descendants.

sentences.zh: 帝晚年深信佛道鬼神，辛巳，始詔「有盜毀佛及天尊、岳、鎮、海、瀆神像者，以不道論；

translations.literal: In his later years the Emperor deeply trusted Buddhism, Daoism, and spirits and ghosts. On the day xinsi, he first issued an edict: "Whoever steals or destroys images of Buddha, the Celestial Worthy, or the spirits of mountains, commanderies, seas, and waterways shall be punished under the statute on heterodoxy;
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the Emperor came to place deep faith in Buddhism, Daoism, and the spirit world. On the day xinsi he issued his first edict on the matter: "Anyone who steals or destroys images of Buddha, the Celestial Worthy, or the spirits of mountains, commanderies, seas, and waterways shall be charged under the statute on heterodoxy;

sentences.zh: 沙門毀佛像，道士毀天尊像者，以惡逆論。

translations.literal: Buddhist monks who destroy Buddha images and Daoist priests who destroy Celestial Worthy images shall be punished under the statute on treacherous rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: If Buddhist monks destroy Buddha images or Daoist priests destroy Celestial Worthy images, they shall be charged under the statute on treacherous rebellion.

sentences.zh: 是歲，征同州刺史蔡王智積入朝。

translations.literal: That year, the Prince of Cai Wang Zhiji, governor of Tongzhou, was summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Emperor summoned Wang Zhiji, Prince of Cai and governor of Tongzhou, to court.

sentences.zh: 智積，帝之弟子也。

translations.literal: Zhiji was the Emperor's younger brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiji was a nephew of the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 性修謹，門無私謁，自奉簡素，帝甚憐之。

translations.literal: By nature disciplined and cautious, his gate received no private visitors; he maintained a frugal way of life for himself, and the Emperor greatly favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Disciplined and cautious by nature, he admitted no private callers at his gate and lived frugally on his own account. The Emperor held him in deep affection.

sentences.zh: 智積有五男，止教讀《論語》、《孝經》，不令交通賓客。

translations.literal: Zhiji had five sons; he only had them study the Analects and the Classic of Filial Piety and did not allow them to associate with guests.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiji had five sons. He had them read only the Analects and the Classic of Filial Piety and forbade them to socialize with visitors.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，智積曰：「卿非知我者！

translations.literal: When someone asked the reason, Zhiji said: "You do not understand me!
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked why, Zhiji said, "You do not truly know me!

sentences.zh: 」其意蓋恐諸子有才能以致禍也。

translations.literal: " His meaning was probably that he feared his sons' talents might bring disaster upon them.
translations.idiomatic: His meaning, in all likelihood, was that he feared his sons' abilities might bring calamity upon them.

sentences.zh: 齊州行參軍章武王伽送流囚李參等七十餘人詣京師，行至滎陽，哀其辛苦，悉呼謂曰：「卿輩自犯國刑，身嬰縲紲，固其職也；

translations.literal: Wang Jia of Zhangwu, Adjunct Militia Officer of Qizhou, was escorting over seventy exiled convicts including Li Can to the capital. Reaching Xingyang, pitying their hardship, he called them all together and said: "You yourselves violated the state's punishments and bear fetters—this is as it should be;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jia of Zhangwu, an adjunct militia officer in Qizhou, was escorting more than seventy exiled convicts, including Li Can, to the capital. When they reached Xingyang, moved by their suffering, he summoned them all and said, "You broke the laws of the state and wear shackles—that is only fitting;

sentences.zh: 重勞援卒，豈不愧心哉！

translations.literal: yet to impose such extra labor on the escort soldiers—are you not ashamed in your hearts?
translations.idiomatic: yet to burden the escort soldiers so heavily—does that not weigh on your conscience?

sentences.zh: 」參等辭謝。

translations.literal: " Li Can and the others apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Li Can and the others apologized.

sentences.zh: 伽乃悉脫其枷鎖，停援卒，與約曰：「某日當至京師，如致前卻，吾當為汝受死。

translations.literal: Jia then removed all their cangues and shackles, dismissed the escorts, and made an agreement with them: "On such-and-such a day you must reach the capital. If you fall behind as before, I will accept death on your behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Jia then removed all their cangues and shackles, dismissed the escort detail, and struck a bargain with them: "You must reach the capital on the appointed day. If any of you lag behind as before, I will die in your place.

sentences.zh: 」遂捨之而去。

translations.literal: " He then released them and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Then he let them go and set out alone.

sentences.zh: 流人感悅，如期而至，一無離叛。

translations.literal: The exiles were moved and pleased; they arrived on schedule, not a single one deserting.
translations.idiomatic: The exiles were deeply moved and kept their word, arriving on time without a single defection.

sentences.zh: 上聞而驚異，召見與語，稱善久之。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard of it and was astonished; he summoned Jia for an audience and spoke with him, praising him at length.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor heard of this he was astonished. He summoned Jia, spoke with him at length, and praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 於是悉召流人，令攜負妻子俱入，賜宴於殿庭而赦之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned all the exiles, had them bring their wives and children inside together, feasted them in the palace hall, and pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned all the exiles, had them enter with their wives and children, feasted them in the palace courtyard, and granted them a general pardon.

sentences.zh: 因下詔曰：「凡在有生，含靈稟性，咸知善惡，並識是非。

translations.literal: He then issued an edict: "All who possess life, endowed with spirit and nature, all know good and evil and likewise discern right from wrong.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued an edict: "Every living being endowed with spirit and nature knows good from evil and can tell right from wrong.

sentences.zh: 若臨以至誠，明加勸導，則俗必從化，人皆遷善。

translations.literal: If one approaches them with utmost sincerity and clearly guides them, custom will surely be transformed and people will all turn toward goodness.
translations.idiomatic: If officials meet them with perfect sincerity and guide them plainly, custom will change and people will turn toward what is good.

sentences.zh: 往以海內亂離，德教廢絕，吏無慈愛之心，民懷奸詐之意。

translations.literal: Formerly, because the realm was torn by disorder, moral instruction was abandoned, officials lacked compassionate hearts, and the people harbored deceitful intentions.
translations.idiomatic: In the past the realm was torn by chaos, moral instruction collapsed, officials had no heart for kindness, and the people nursed deceit in their breasts.

sentences.zh: 朕思遵聖法，以德化民，而伽深識朕意，誠心宣導，參等感悟，自赴憲司：明是率土之人，非為難教。

translations.literal: I think to follow the sage's law and transform the people through virtue. Jia deeply understood my intent and sincerely proclaimed and guided them; Li Can and his companions were moved to awareness and presented themselves to the law office—showing clearly that all people under Heaven are not hard to teach.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to follow the way of the sages and transform the people through virtue. Jia understood my purpose deeply and preached it in earnest; Li Can and his companions were moved to repentance and surrendered themselves to the authorities. This shows that the people of the realm are not beyond teaching.

sentences.zh: 若使官盡王伽之儔，民皆李參之輩，刑厝不用，其何遠哉！

translations.literal: If all officials were like Wang Jia and all people like Li Can, punishments could be set aside unused—how far off would that be!
translations.idiomatic: If every official were a Wang Jia and every subject a Li Can, punishments could be laid aside altogether. How far off is such an age!

sentences.zh: 」乃擢伽為雍令。

translations.literal: " He then promoted Jia to magistrate of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: With that he promoted Jia to magistrate of Yong.

sentences.zh: 太史令袁充表稱：「隋興已後，晝日漸長，開皇元年，冬至之景長一丈二尺七寸二分；

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Yuan Chong memorialized: "Since the rise of Sui, daylight has gradually lengthened. In the first year of Kaihuang, the shadow at the winter solstice was one zhang, two chi, seven cun, and two fen long;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologer Yuan Chong submitted a memorial stating: "Since the founding of Sui, the daylight hours have steadily lengthened. In the first year of Kaihuang the noon shadow at the winter solstice measured one zhang, two chi, seven cun, and two fen;

sentences.zh: 自爾漸短，至十七年，短於舊三寸七分。

translations.literal: since then it has gradually shortened; by the seventeenth year it was three cun and seven fen shorter than before.
translations.idiomatic: from that point it has grown shorter year by year, until in the seventeenth year it fell three cun and seven fen below the earlier measure.

sentences.zh: 日去極近則景短而日長，去極遠則景長而日短；

translations.literal: When the sun is near the pole, the shadow is short and the day is long; when far from the pole, the shadow is long and the day is short;
translations.idiomatic: When the sun draws near the celestial pole the shadow shortens and the day lengthens; when it draws far from the pole the shadow lengthens and the day shortens.

sentences.zh: 行內道則去極近，行外道則去極遠。

translations.literal: traveling the inner path draws near the pole; traveling the outer path draws far from it.
translations.idiomatic: Travel along the inner path brings the sun nearer the pole; travel along the outer path takes it farther away.

sentences.zh: 謹按《元命包》云：『日月出內道，璇璣得其常。

translations.literal: Respectfully consulting the Yuanming Bao, it says: 'When sun and moon emerge on the inner path, the celestial pivot maintains its constancy.'
translations.idiomatic: I have carefully consulted the Yuanming Bao, which says: 'When sun and moon travel the inner path, the celestial pivot keeps its proper order.'

sentences.zh: 』《京房別對》曰：『太平，日行上道；

translations.literal: ' The Jingfang Bie Dui says: 'In an age of great peace the sun travels the upper path;
translations.idiomatic: The Jingfang Bie Dui states: 'In an age of supreme peace the sun travels the upper path;

sentences.zh: 昇平，行次道；

translations.literal: in an age of rising peace it travels the middle path;
translations.idiomatic: in an age of modest peace it travels the middle path;

sentences.zh: 霸代，行下道。

translations.literal: in an age of hegemony it travels the lower path.'
translations.idiomatic: in an age of mere hegemony it travels the lower path.'

sentences.zh: 』伏惟大隋啟運，上感乾元，景短日長，振古希有。

translations.literal: ' I respectfully consider that great Sui has received the Mandate, moved by the virtue of Heaven; short shadows and long days are rarely seen since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: ' I respectfully submit that great Sui has received the Mandate, stirred by the power of Heaven itself. Shadows growing shorter and days growing longer are a wonder seldom seen since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 」上臨朝，謂百官曰：「景長之慶，天之祐也。

translations.literal: " The Emperor held court and said to the hundred officials: "The blessing of lengthening shadows is Heaven's protection.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor held court and told the assembled officials, "This blessing of lengthening days is Heaven's favor upon us.

sentences.zh: 今太子新立，當須改元，宜取日長之意以為年號。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince has newly been established; we must change the era name. We should take the meaning of lengthening days as the era name.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince has just been installed, so the era name must be changed. Let us take the meaning of lengthening days for the new reign title.

sentences.zh: 」是後百工作役，並加程課，以日長故也。

translations.literal: " Thereafter corvée labor for all construction projects had increased quotas added, because of the lengthened days.
translations.idiomatic: After that, quotas on corvée labor for every public works project were increased on the grounds that the days had grown longer.

sentences.zh: 丁匠苦之。

translations.literal: The corvée craftsmen suffered from this.
translations.idiomatic: The drafted craftsmen were driven to misery by it.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙酉朔，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day yiyou, the first of the month, he pardoned all under Heaven and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on yiyou—the first day of the month—the Emperor pardoned the empire and changed the reign title.

sentences.zh: 以尚書右僕射楊素為左僕射，納言蘇威為右僕射。

translations.literal: Yang Su, Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, was made Left Vice Director; Su Wei, Palace Attendant, was made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su, Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, was appointed Left Vice Director; Su Wei, Director of the Palace Secretariat, was appointed Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，徙河南王昭為晉王。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, Prince Zhao of Henan was transferred to be Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Prince Zhao of Henan was reassigned as Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 突厥步迦可汗犯塞，敗代州總管韓弘於恆安。

translations.literal: Tujue Qaghan Boka invaded the frontier; he defeated Han Hong, military governor of Daizhou, at Heng'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Tujue qaghan Boka raided the frontier and defeated Han Hong, military governor of Daizhou, at Heng'an.

sentences.zh: 以晉王昭為內史令。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao of Jin was appointed Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhao of Jin was appointed Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙卯朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day yimao, the first of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yimao—the first day of the month—there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，己丑，突厥男女九萬口來降。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on the day jichou, ninety thousand Tujue men and women came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on jichou, ninety thousand Tujue men and women surrendered.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙卯，遣十六使巡省風俗。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day yimao, he dispatched sixteen envoys to tour and inspect local customs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on yimao, he sent out sixteen envoys to tour the provinces and inspect local customs.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，詔以天下學校生徒多而不精，唯簡留國子學生七十人，太學、四門及州縣學並廢。

translations.literal: On the day yichou, an edict stated that students in schools throughout the realm were numerous but unrefined; only seventy students at the Directorate of Education would be retained, and the Imperial Academy, Four Gates School, and prefectural and county schools were all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou an edict declared that students in schools across the empire were too many and too poorly trained. Only seventy students at the Directorate of Education were to be kept; the Imperial Academy, the Four Gates School, and all prefectural and county schools were abolished.

sentences.zh: 前殿內將軍河間劉炫上表切諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Former Palace Interior General Liu Xuan of Hejian submitted a memorial urgently remonstrating; the Emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Former Palace Interior General Liu Xuan of Hejian submitted a forceful memorial in protest, but the Emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊戌，改國子學為太學。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day wuxu, the Directorate of Education was renamed the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on wuxu, the Directorate of Education was renamed the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 初，帝受周禪，恐民心未服，故多稱符瑞以耀之，其偽造而獻者，不可勝計。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor received the abdication from Zhou, fearing the people's hearts were not yet won over, he frequently proclaimed portents and auspicious omens to display his mandate; those who fabricated and presented them were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Emperor accepted the Zhou abdication, he feared the people were not yet won over, so he repeatedly proclaimed portents and auspicious signs to burnish his mandate. Those who forged such omens and presented them were beyond number.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，己丑，有事於南郊，如封禪禮，板文備述前後符瑞以報謝雲。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on the day jichou, he performed rites at the Southern Altar, following the form of the Feng and Shan sacrifices; the wooden inscription fully recounted portents before and after to give thanks to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on jichou, he performed rites at the Southern Altar in the manner of the Feng and Shan sacrifices. The wooden inscription set forth the portents of earlier and later times in full, offering thanks to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 山獠作亂，以衛尉少卿洛陽衛文昇為資州刺史鎮撫之。

translations.literal: Mountain Liao tribes rebelled; Palace Defender Commandant Wei Wensheng of Luoyang was appointed governor of Zizhou to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain Liao rose in rebellion. Wei Wensheng of Luoyang, Deputy Director of the Palace Guard, was appointed governor of Zizhou to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 文昇名玄，以字行。

translations.literal: Wensheng's given name was Xuan; he was known by his style name.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng's personal name was Xuan; he was known by his style name.

sentences.zh: 初到官，獠方攻大牢鎮，文昇單騎造其營，謂曰：「我是刺史，銜天子詔，安養汝等，勿驚懼也！

translations.literal: Upon first reaching his post, while the Liao were attacking Dalaozhen, Wensheng rode alone to their camp and said: "I am the governor, bearing the Son of Heaven's edict to comfort and nourish you—do not be alarmed or afraid!
translations.idiomatic: When he first took office the Liao were attacking Dalaozhen. Wensheng rode alone into their camp and said, "I am your governor. I come bearing the Son of Heaven's command to protect and provide for you. Do not be afraid!

sentences.zh: 」群獠莫敢動。

translations.literal: " The assembled Liao dared not stir.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao host did not dare move.

sentences.zh: 於是說以利害，渠帥感悅，解兵而去，前後歸附者十餘萬口。

translations.literal: Thereupon he explained advantages and disadvantages; the chieftains were moved and pleased, dismissed their troops and departed, and those who submitted before and after numbered over one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He then explained what they stood to gain or lose. The chieftains were won over, laid down their arms, and withdrew. In all, more than one hundred thousand submitted before and after.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賜縑二千匹。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed two thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was delighted and rewarded him with two thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以文昇為遂州總管。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, Wensheng was made military governor of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Wensheng was appointed military governor of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 潮、成等五州獠反，高州酋長馮盎馳詣京師，請討之。

translations.literal: The Liao of five prefectures including Chao and Cheng rebelled; Feng Ang, chieftain of Gaozhou, hurried to the capital to request permission to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao of five prefectures, including Chao and Cheng, rebelled. Feng Ang, chieftain of Gaozhou, raced to the capital and asked leave to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 帝敕楊素與盎論賊形勢，素歎曰：「不意蠻夷中有如是人！

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Yang Su to discuss the rebels' situation with Ang; Su sighed and said: "I had not expected such a man among the barbarian tribes!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Yang Su to discuss the rebels' situation with Feng Ang. Su sighed and said, "I never imagined such a man could be found among the frontier peoples!

sentences.zh: 」即遣盎發江、嶺兵擊之。

translations.literal: " He immediately dispatched Ang to mobilize troops from the Jiang and Ling regions to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sent Feng Ang to raise troops from the Jiang and Ling regions and strike the rebels.

sentences.zh: 事平，除盎漢陽太守。

translations.literal: When the matter was settled, Ang was appointed Administrator of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign was over, Feng Ang was appointed administrator of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 詔以楊素為雲州道行軍元帥，長孫晟為受降使者，挾啟民可汗北擊步迦。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Yang Su commander-in-chief of the Yunzhou campaign route; Changsun Sheng was made envoy to receive surrenders; together with Qimin Qaghan they marched north to attack Boka.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named Yang Su commander-in-chief on the Yunzhou campaign route, appointed Changsun Sheng envoy for receiving surrenders, and ordered them to march north with Qimin Qaghan to attack Boka.

sentences.zh: 春，三月，己亥，上幸仁壽宮。

translations.literal: In spring, the third month, on the day jihai, the Emperor visited Renshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the third month, on jihai, the Emperor went to Renshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 突厥思力俟斤等南渡河，掠啟民男女六千口、雜畜二十餘萬而去。

translations.literal: Tujue Silijin and others crossed the river south, plundered six thousand men and women belonging to Qimin and over two hundred thousand assorted livestock, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The Tujue leader Silijin and others crossed the river to the south, seized six thousand of Qimin's men and women and more than two hundred thousand head of mixed livestock, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 楊素帥諸軍追擊，轉戰六十餘里，大破之，突厥北走。

translations.literal: Yang Su led the armies in pursuit, fought for over sixty li, routed them completely, and the Tujue fled north.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su led the army in pursuit, fought them for more than sixty li, and routed them completely. The Tujue fled north.

sentences.zh: 素復進追，夜，及之，恐其越逸，令其騎稍後，親引兩騎並降突厥二人與虜並行，虜不之覺；

translations.literal: Su again pressed the pursuit; at night he caught up, fearing they would escape across the frontier. He had his cavalry hang back slightly, personally led two horsemen along with two surrendered Tujue to march alongside the enemy camp—the enemy did not notice;
translations.idiomatic: Su pressed on again. By night he caught up with them, but feared they would escape beyond reach. He held his cavalry back a little, then personally took two riders and two surrendered Tujue and rode alongside the enemy column. The enemy did not notice.

sentences.zh: 候其頓捨未定，趣後騎掩擊，大破之，悉得人畜以歸啟民。

translations.literal: waiting until their encampment was not yet settled, he urged the rear cavalry to launch a surprise attack, routed them utterly, and recovered all people and livestock to return to Qimin.
translations.idiomatic: When their camp was not yet fully settled, he signaled the cavalry behind him to strike. He broke them completely, recovered all the people and livestock, and restored them to Qimin.

sentences.zh: 自是突厥遠遁，磧南無復寇抄。

translations.literal: From this the Tujue fled far away, and south of the desert there were no more raids.
translations.idiomatic: After that the Tujue withdrew far to the north, and south of the desert there were no more raids.

sentences.zh: 素以功進子玄感柱國，賜玄縱爵淮南公。

translations.literal: For his merit Su had his son Xuangan advanced to Pillar of State and bestowed upon Su Xuanzong the title Marquis of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement Su had his son Xuangan promoted to Pillar of State and granted his son Xuanzong the title Marquis of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書柳述，慶之孫也，尚蘭陵公主，怙寵使氣，自楊素之屬皆下之。

translations.literal: Minister of War Liu Shu, grandson of Liu Qing, married Princess Lanling; relying on favor he was overbearing, and even men of Yang Su's rank bowed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shu, Minister of War and grandson of Liu Qing, had married Princess Lanling. Swollen with imperial favor, he threw his weight about arrogantly, and even men of Yang Su's stature deferred to him.

sentences.zh: 帝問符璽直長萬年韋雲起：「外間有不便事，可言之。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Wei Yunqi, Direct Clerk of Seals and Credentials of Wannian: "Are there inconvenient matters abroad? You may speak of them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked Wei Yunqi, Direct Clerk of Seals and Credentials from Wannian, "If there is anything amiss in the realm, speak of it.

sentences.zh: 」述時侍側，雲起奏曰：「柳述驕豪，未嘗經事，兵機要重，非其所堪。

translations.literal: " Yang Shu was attending at his side. Yunqi memorialized: "Liu Shu is arrogant and overbearing; he has never handled affairs; military matters are critically important and not what he can bear.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Shu was standing beside him. Yunqi replied, "Liu Shu is proud and domineering. He has never managed serious business. Military affairs are weighty matters, and he is not equal to them.

sentences.zh: 徒以主婿，遂居要職。

translations.literal: He holds a crucial post only because he is the emperor's son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: He holds a high post only because he is the emperor's son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 臣恐物議以陛下為『官不擇賢，專私所愛』，斯亦不便之大者。

translations.literal: I fear public opinion will take Your Majesty to be one who 'does not select officials by merit but favors those he personally loves'—this too is a great inconvenience.
translations.idiomatic: I fear people will say of Your Majesty that you 'appoint men not for talent but for private affection.' That would be a grave evil in its own right.

sentences.zh: 」帝甚然其言，顧謂述曰：「雲起之言，汝藥石也，可師友之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor greatly approved his words, turned to Shu and said: "Yunqi's words are medicine and whetstone for you—you should take him as teacher and friend.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor strongly agreed. Turning to Liu Shu he said, "Yunqi's words are medicine and whetstone for you. Treat him as a teacher and friend.

sentences.zh: 」秋，七月，丙戌，詔內外官各舉所知。

translations.literal: " In autumn, the seventh month, on the day bingxu, an edict ordered inner and outer officials each to recommend men they knew.
translations.idiomatic: " In autumn, the seventh month, on bingxu, an edict ordered officials throughout the government each to recommend men they knew.

sentences.zh: 柳述舉雲起，除通事舍人。

translations.literal: Liu Shu recommended Yunqi, who was appointed Master of Communications.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shu recommended Yunqi, who was appointed Master of Communications.

sentences.zh: 益州總管蜀王秀，容貌瑰偉，有膽氣，好武藝。

translations.literal: Prince Xiu of Shu, military governor of Yizhou, had a magnificent and imposing appearance, courage, and loved martial arts.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiu of Shu, military governor of Yizhou, was striking in appearance, bold in spirit, and devoted to martial arts.

sentences.zh: 帝每謂獨孤-{后}-曰：「秀必以惡終，我在當無慮，至兄弟，必反矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor often said to Empress Dugu: "Xiu will surely come to a bad end. While I live there need be no worry, but when it comes to his brothers, he will surely rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor often told Empress Dugu, "Xiu is bound to end badly. While I am alive there is nothing to fear, but once it comes to his brothers, he will surely rebel.

sentences.zh: 」大將軍劉噲之討西爨也，帝令上開府儀同三司楊武通將兵繼進。

translations.literal: " When Grand General Liu Yan was campaigning against the Western Cuan, the Emperor ordered Yang Wutong, a General-in-Chief with Honorary Second Rank, to lead troops in continued advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand General Liu Yan was campaigning against the Western Cuan, the Emperor ordered Yang Wutong, a general of the second rank with honorary third rank, to follow with reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 秀以嬖人萬智光為武通行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Xiu appointed his favorite Wan Zhiguang as Wutong's campaign marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu appointed his favorite Wan Zhiguang as campaign marshal under Yang Wutong.

sentences.zh: 帝以秀任非其人，譴責之，因謂群臣曰：「壞我法者，子孫也。

translations.literal: The Emperor, thinking Xiu had appointed an unworthy man, rebuked and censured him, then said to the assembled ministers: "Those who ruin my laws are my own sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor judged that Xiu had put the wrong man in place, rebuked him sharply, and then told the assembled ministers, "Those who wreck my laws are my own sons and grandsons.

sentences.zh: 譬如猛虎，物不能害，反為毛間蟲所損食耳。

translations.literal: It is like a fierce tiger—no creature can harm it, yet it is gnawed and consumed by insects in its fur."
translations.idiomatic: It is like a tiger: nothing in the wild can hurt it, yet it is eaten away by the lice in its fur."

sentences.zh: 」遂分秀所統。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he divided the forces under Xiu's command.
translations.idiomatic: He then stripped Xiu of part of his command.

sentences.zh: 自長史元巖卒後，秀漸奢僭，造渾天儀，多捕山獠充宦者，車馬被服，擬於乘輿。

translations.literal: After Chief Administrator Yuan Yan died, Xiu gradually grew extravagant and presumptuous; he constructed an armillary sphere, captured many mountain Liao to serve as eunuchs, and his carriages, horses, and attire rivaled the imperial equipage.
translations.idiomatic: After Chief Administrator Yuan Yan died, Xiu grew increasingly extravagant and overstepped his rank. He built an armillary sphere, seized many mountain Liao to serve as eunuchs, and equipped his carriages, horses, and robes in imitation of the imperial train.

sentences.zh: 及太子勇以讒廢，晉王廣為太子，秀意甚不平。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Yong was deposed through slander and Prince Guang of Jin became Crown Prince, Xiu was deeply discontented.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Yong was deposed on false charges and Prince Guang of Jin became heir, Xiu was deeply resentful.

sentences.zh: 太子恐秀終為後患，陰令楊素求其罪而譖之。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince, fearing Xiu would ultimately become a future threat, secretly ordered Yang Su to seek out his offenses and slander him.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince, fearing Xiu would become a lasting threat, secretly ordered Yang Su to hunt for offenses with which to denounce him.

sentences.zh: 上遂征秀，秀猶豫，欲謝病不行。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon summoned Xiu; Xiu hesitated and wished to plead illness and not go.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then summoned Xiu to court. Xiu hesitated and wanted to plead illness and stay away.

sentences.zh: 總管司馬源師諫，秀作色曰：「此自我家事，何預卿也！

translations.literal: Chief Administrator's aide Yuan Shi remonstrated; Xiu flushed with anger and said: "This is my own family affair—what concern is it of yours!
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator's aide Yuan Shi remonstrated with him. Xiu's face darkened and he said, "This is my own family's business. What business is it of yours!

sentences.zh: 」師垂涕對曰：「師忝參府幕，敢不盡心！

translations.literal: " Shi, tears streaming, replied: "Shi humbly serves in your headquarters—how would I dare not give my whole heart!
translations.idiomatic: " Shi replied through tears, "I am honored to serve in Your Highness's headquarters. How could I fail to give you my utmost counsel!

sentences.zh: 聖上有敕追王，以淹時月，今乃遷延未去。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven has issued an order summoning Your Highness; months have passed, yet now you delay and have not departed.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven has issued an order summoning you. Months have already passed, yet you still linger and have not set out.

sentences.zh: 百姓不識王心，倘生異議，內外疑駭，發雷霆之詔，降一介之使，王何以自明？

translations.literal: The common people do not understand Your Highness's intent; if dissent arises, inner and outer circles grow suspicious and alarmed—a thunderous edict is issued and a single envoy dispatched—how will Your Highness clear yourself?
translations.idiomatic: The common people cannot read Your Highness's mind. If they take alarm, suspicion will spread inside and out. When a thunderous edict arrives and a single envoy is sent, how will you prove your innocence?

sentences.zh: 願王熟計之！

translations.literal: I beg Your Highness to think this through carefully!
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Highness to weigh this carefully!

sentences.zh: 」朝廷恐秀生變，戊子，以原州總管獨孤楷為益州總管，馳傳代之。

translations.literal: " The court, fearing Xiu might cause trouble, on the day wuzi appointed Dugu Kai, military governor of Yuanzhou, to replace him as governor of Yizhou, traveling by relay post.
translations.idiomatic: " The court, fearing Xiu might rebel, on wuzi appointed Dugu Kai, military governor of Yuanzhou, to replace him as governor of Yizhou and sent him posthaste.

sentences.zh: 楷至，秀猶未肯行；

translations.literal: When Kai arrived, Xiu still was unwilling to depart;
translations.idiomatic: When Kai arrived, Xiu still refused to leave;

sentences.zh: 楷諷諭久之，乃就路。

translations.literal: Kai admonished and persuaded him at length before he finally set out on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Kai admonished him at length before he finally took to the road.

sentences.zh: 楷察秀有悔色，因勒兵為備；

translations.literal: Kai perceived that Xiu had a regretful look, and therefore ordered troops drawn up as a precaution;
translations.idiomatic: Kai saw regret on Xiu's face and therefore kept his troops under arms as a precaution;

sentences.zh: 秀行四十餘里，將還襲楷，覘知有備，乃止。

translations.literal: Xiu traveled over forty li, was about to turn back and attack Kai, but spying that preparations had been made, stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu had gone more than forty li when he was about to turn back and attack Kai, but seeing that Kai was on guard, he abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 八月，甲子，皇后獨孤氏崩。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day jiazi, Empress Dugu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiazi, Empress Dugu died.

sentences.zh: 太子對上及宮人哀慟絕氣，若不勝喪者；

translations.literal: Before the Emperor and the palace women the Crown Prince mourned in such violent grief that he seemed on the verge of breathlessness, as one unable to bear the loss;
translations.idiomatic: In the Emperor's presence and before the palace women, the Crown Prince wept and wailed until he seemed barely able to breathe, as though crushed by grief;

sentences.zh: 其處私室，飲食言笑如平常。

translations.literal: In his private chambers, he ate, drank, spoke, and laughed as in ordinary times.
translations.idiomatic: In private his meals, conversation, and laughter were no different from before.

sentences.zh: 又，每朝令進二溢米，而私令外取肥肉脯鮓，置竹桶中，以蠟閉口，衣袱裹而納之。

translations.literal: Moreover, each morning he ordered only two sheng of rice to be brought, but privately had fatty meat, dried meat, and pickled fish fetched from outside, placed them in a bamboo bucket, sealed the mouth with wax, wrapped it in a cloth bundle, and had it brought in.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning he publicly ordered only two sheng of rice, but secretly had rich meats, dried flesh, and pickled fish smuggled in inside a wax-sealed bamboo bucket wrapped in cloth.

sentences.zh: 著作郎王劭上言：「佛說：『人應生天上及生無量壽國之時，天佛放大光明，以香花妓樂來迎。

translations.literal: Editorial Director Wang Shao memorialized the throne: "The Buddha says: 'When a person is destined to be born in heaven or in the Land of Immeasurable Life, heaven and Buddha send forth great radiant light and come to welcome him with incense, flowers, singing girls, and music.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial Director Wang Shao submitted a memorial: "The Buddha teaches that when one is destined for heaven or for the Land of Immeasurable Life, heaven and Buddha pour forth great light and come to welcome the soul with incense, flowers, dancers, and music.

sentences.zh: 』伏惟大行皇后福善禎符，備諸秘記，皆雲是妙善菩薩。

translations.literal: ' I humbly consider that the late Empress's blessed virtue and auspicious signs, recorded fully in secret texts, all say she was the Bodhisattva Miaoshan.
translations.idiomatic: "Your late Empress, blessed in merit and graced by omens recorded in many secret texts, is everywhere said to have been the Bodhisattva Miaoshan.

sentences.zh: 臣謹案八月二十二日，仁壽官內再雨金銀花；

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully notes that on the twenty-second day of the eighth month, gold and silver flowers again rained within Renshou Palace;
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully report that on the twenty-second day of the eighth month, flowers of gold and silver fell twice within Renshou Palace;

sentences.zh: 二十三日，大寶殿後夜有神光；

translations.literal: On the twenty-third, divine light appeared behind the Hall of Great Treasure during the latter half of the night;
translations.idiomatic: on the twenty-third, a supernatural light appeared behind the Hall of Great Treasure in the deep hours of the night;

sentences.zh: 二十四日卯時，永安宮北有自然種種音樂，震滿虛空；

translations.literal: On the twenty-fourth, at the hour of mao, various kinds of spontaneous music appeared north of Yong'an Palace, shaking and filling the empty sky;
translations.idiomatic: on the twenty-fourth, at dawn, unearthly music of every kind rang north of Yong'an Palace, reverberating through the heavens;

sentences.zh: 至夜五更，奄然如寐，遂即升遐，與經文所說，事皆符驗。

translations.literal: Reaching the fifth watch of the night, she suddenly fell as if asleep and thereupon ascended to the far realm; all these things match and verify what the scriptures describe.
translations.idiomatic: and by the fifth watch of the night she had quietly passed away as though in sleep—every sign matching the scriptures' description.

sentences.zh: 」上覽之悲喜。

translations.literal: " When the Emperor read it he felt both joy and grief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor read the memorial, he was moved both to joy and to sorrow.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙戌，上至自仁壽宮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day bingxu, the Emperor arrived back from Renshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day bingxu, the Emperor returned from Renshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸丑，以工部尚書楊達為納言。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day guichou, Minister of Works Yang Da was appointed Nayan.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the day guichou, Yang Da, Minister of Works, was appointed Nayan.

sentences.zh: 達，雄之弟也。

translations.literal: Da was the younger brother of Yang Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Da was the younger brother of Yang Xiong.

sentences.zh: 閏月，甲申，詔楊素、蘇威與吏部尚書牛弘等修定五禮。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the day jiashen, an edict ordered Yang Su, Su Wei, Minister of Personnel Niu Hong, and others to revise and fix the Five Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the day jiashen, the Emperor ordered Yang Su, Su Wei, Minister of Personnel Niu Hong, and others to compile and codify the Five Rites.

sentences.zh: 上令上儀同三司蕭吉為皇后擇葬地，得吉處，云：「卜年二千，卜世二百。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Superior Yitong Third Rank Xiao Ji to select a burial site for the Empress; finding an auspicious place, he said: "Divined years: two thousand; divined generations: two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor charged Superior Yitong Third Rank Xiao Ji to find a burial site for the Empress. Ji chose an auspicious spot and declared, "Divination shows two thousand years of blessing and two hundred generations of rule."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「吉凶由人，不在於地。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Good fortune and ill lie in men, not in the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied, "Fortune and ruin depend on men, not on the ground.

sentences.zh: 高緯葬父，豈不卜乎！

translations.literal: When Gao Wei buried his father, did he not perform divination!
translations.idiomatic: Did Gao Wei not divine when he buried his father?

sentences.zh: 俄而國亡。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward his state perished.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his realm was lost within a few years.

sentences.zh: 正如我家墓田，若雲不吉，朕不當為天子；

translations.literal: Just so with my family's ancestral grave lands—if one says they were inauspicious, I ought not to have become Son of Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Consider my own family tombs: if they were truly inauspicious, I should never have become emperor;

sentences.zh: 若雲不凶，我弟不當戰沒。

translations.literal: if one says they were not inauspicious, my younger brother ought not to have died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: if they were auspicious, my brother should not have fallen in battle.

sentences.zh: 」然竟從吉言。

translations.literal: " Yet in the end he still followed Ji's words.
translations.idiomatic: Nevertheless he accepted Ji's reading in the end.

sentences.zh: 吉退，告族人蕭平仲曰：「皇太子遣宇文左率深謝余云：『公前稱我當為太子，竟有其驗，終不忘也。

translations.literal: When Ji withdrew, he told his clansman Xiao Pingzhong: "The Crown Prince sent the Left Commander of the Yuwen Household to express deep thanks to me, saying: 'You formerly said I would become Crown Prince, and it has indeed come to pass; I shall never forget it.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Ji told his kinsman Xiao Pingzhong, "The Crown Prince sent the Left Commander of the Yuwen Household to thank me deeply. He said, 'You once foretold that I would be Crown Prince, and you were right. I shall never forget it.

sentences.zh: 今卜山陵，務令我早立。

translations.literal: Now in divining the imperial tomb, see that I am enthroned early.
translations.idiomatic: Now that you are divining the imperial tomb, see to it that I am enthroned without delay.

sentences.zh: 我立之後，當以富貴相報。

translations.literal: After I am enthroned, I shall reward you with wealth and rank.'
translations.idiomatic: Once I reign, I will repay you with wealth and honor.'

sentences.zh: 』吾語之曰：『後四載，太子御天下。

translations.literal: I told him: 'In four years' time the Crown Prince will rule all under Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: I answered him, 'In four years the Crown Prince will take the throne.'

sentences.zh: 』若太子得政，隋其亡乎！

translations.literal: If the Crown Prince gains power, will Sui perish!
translations.idiomatic: If the Crown Prince comes to power, Sui is doomed!

sentences.zh: 吾前紿云『卜年二千』者，三十字也；

translations.literal: My earlier deception of saying 'two thousand years of divination' meant thirty characters;
translations.idiomatic: When I said 'two thousand years of divination,' I was deceiving him—thirty is the number I meant;

sentences.zh: 『卜世二百』者，取世二傳也。

translations.literal: 'two hundred generations of divination' meant only two generations of transmission.
translations.idiomatic: and 'two hundred generations' meant only two reigns passed down.

sentences.zh: 汝其識之！

translations.literal: You must remember this!
translations.idiomatic: Mark this well!

sentences.zh: 壬寅，葬文獻皇后於太陵。

translations.literal: On the day renyin, Empress Wenxian was buried at Tailing.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renyin, Empress Wenxian was interred at Tailing.

sentences.zh: 詔以「楊素經營葬事，勤求吉地，論素此心，事極誠孝，豈與夫平戎定寇比其功業！

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Yang Su managed the burial affairs, diligently seeking an auspicious site; considering Su's intent in this matter, his devotion and filial piety were supreme—is this to be compared with pacifying barbarians and settling invaders as to merit!
translations.idiomatic: An edict proclaimed that Yang Su, in directing the burial and tirelessly seeking an auspicious site, had shown a devotion and filial piety beyond anything owed for pacifying frontier enemies—

sentences.zh: 可別封一子義康公，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: One of his sons may be separately enfeoffed as Duke of Yikang, with a fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: one of his sons was to be enfeoffed separately as Duke of Yikang with ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 」並賜田三十頃，絹萬段，米萬石，金珠綾錦稱是。

translations.literal: " He was also granted thirty qing of fields, ten thousand bolts of silk, ten thousand shi of grain, and gold, pearls, brocade, and fine silk in corresponding measure.
translations.idiomatic: He also received thirty qing of fields, ten thousand bolts of silk, ten thousand shi of grain, and gold, pearls, brocades, and fine silks in proportion.

sentences.zh: 蜀王秀至長安，上見之，不與語；

translations.literal: When the Prince of Shu, Xiu, reached Chang'an, the Emperor saw him but did not speak with him;
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Shu Yang Xiu arrived at Chang'an, the Emperor received him but refused to speak;

sentences.zh: 明日，使使切讓之。

translations.literal: The next day he sent an envoy to rebuke him sternly.
translations.idiomatic: The following day he sent an envoy to reprimand him sharply.

sentences.zh: 秀謝罪，太子諸王流涕庭謝。

translations.literal: Xiu begged forgiveness; the Crown Prince and the other princes wept and begged pardon in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu pleaded guilty, and the Crown Prince and the other princes wept as they begged forgiveness in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「頃者秦王糜費財物，我以父道訓之。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Recently the Prince of Qin wasted goods and wealth; I admonished him in the way of a father.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "When the Prince of Qin squandered wealth, I corrected him as a father would a son.

sentences.zh: 今秀蠹害生民，當以君道繩之。

translations.literal: Now Xiu harms and injures the people; he must be bound by the way of a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: But Xiu has preyed upon the people. He must be judged as a prince who betrayed the duties of rule."

sentences.zh: 」於是付執法者。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was handed over to the law officers.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was then handed over to the law officers.

sentences.zh: 開府儀同三司慶整諫曰：「庶人勇既廢，秦王已薨，陛下見子無多，何至如是！

translations.literal: Defender-in-Chief Qing Zheng remonstrated: "The commoner Yong has already been deposed, and the Prince of Qin has already died; Your Majesty's surviving sons are not many—why go this far!
translations.idiomatic: Defender-in-Chief Qing Zheng protested, "The deposed Prince Yong is gone, and the Prince of Qin is dead. Your Majesty has few sons left—why treat this one so harshly?

sentences.zh: 蜀王性甚耿介，今被重責，恐不自全。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shu is by nature very upright and unyielding; now that he bears heavy blame, I fear he may not preserve himself."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shu is proud and uncompromising. Under such punishment he may not survive."

sentences.zh: 」上大怒，欲斷其舌，因謂群臣曰：「當斬秀於市以謝百姓。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was greatly enraged and wished to cut out his tongue; then he said to the assembled officials: "We should execute Xiu in the marketplace to appease the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flew into a rage and wanted to cut out Qing Zheng's tongue. He told the court, "Xiu should be beheaded in the marketplace to answer for the harm he has done the people."

sentences.zh: 」乃令楊素等推治之。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Yang Su and others to investigate and try the case.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yang Su and others to investigate and prosecute the case.

sentences.zh: 太子陰作偶人，縛手釘心，枷鎖杻械，書上及漢王姓名，仍云「請西嶽慈父聖母神兵收楊堅、楊諒神魂，如此形狀，勿令散蕩。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince secretly made dolls, bound their hands and nailed their hearts, put them in cangues, fetters, and pillories, wrote on them the names of the Emperor and the Prince of Han, and added: "We implore the divine soldiers of the Merciful Father and Holy Mother of the Western Peak to seize the souls of Yang Jian and Yang Liang; keep them in this form and do not let them scatter."
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince secretly fashioned dolls with bound hands and nails driven through their hearts, fitted with cangues, chains, and stocks. On them he wrote the Emperor's name and that of Prince of Han Yang Liang, adding, "We beg the divine army of the Merciful Father and Holy Mother of the Western Peak to seize the souls of Yang Jian and Yang Liang and hold them in this form, that they may not escape."

sentences.zh: 」密埋之華山下，楊素發之；

translations.literal: " He secretly buried them beneath Mount Hua, and Yang Su unearthed them;
translations.idiomatic: He buried them secretly beneath Mount Hua, where Yang Su later dug them up;

sentences.zh: 又雲秀妄述圖讖，稱京師妖異，造蜀地征祥；

translations.literal: it was also charged that Xiu had rashly recounted prognostic texts, speaking of strange omens in the capital and fashioning auspicious signs for Shu;
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was also accused of spreading prognostic texts, proclaiming ominous signs in the capital and inventing favorable omens for Shu;

sentences.zh: 並作檄文，云「指期問罪」，置秀集中，俱以聞奏。

translations.literal: and that he had also written a proclamation saying "We will fix a date to demand accountability"; all these were found among Xiu's papers and reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: and of drafting a proclamation vowing to "call him to account on a set day." All were found among Xiu's papers and reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「天下寧有是邪！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Can such things truly exist under Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor exclaimed, "Can such things truly exist in this realm?

sentences.zh: 」十二月，癸巳，廢秀為庶人，幽之內侍省，不聽與妻子相見，唯獠婢二人驅使，連坐者百餘人。

translations.literal: " In the twelfth month, on the day guisi, Xiu was deposed as a commoner and confined in the Directorate of Palace Attendants; he was not permitted to see his wife and children, only two Liao slave girls were assigned to serve him, and more than a hundred persons were implicated by association.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day guisi, Xiu was stripped of princely rank and confined in the Directorate of Palace Attendants, forbidden to see his wife or children. Only two tribal servant girls attended him. More than a hundred others were punished as accessories.

sentences.zh: 秀上表摧謝曰：「伏願慈恩，賜垂矜愍，殘息未盡之間，希與瓜子相見；

translations.literal: Xiu submitted a memorial in abject apology: "I humbly hope for merciful grace and beg for compassionate pity; while my lingering breath is not yet exhausted, I hope to see Guazi;
translations.idiomatic: Xiu submitted a broken plea for mercy: "I beg Your Majesty's compassion. While I still draw breath, let me see Guazi once more;

sentences.zh: 請賜一穴，令骸骨有所。

translations.literal: I pray that a burial place may be granted, that my bones may have a resting place."
translations.idiomatic: and grant me a grave, that my bones may have somewhere to rest."

sentences.zh: 」瓜子，其愛子也。

translations.literal: " Guazi was his beloved son.
translations.idiomatic: Guazi was the name of his beloved son.

sentences.zh: 上因下詔數其十罪，且曰：「我今不知楊堅、楊諒是汝何親？

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon issued an edict enumerating his ten crimes, and said: "Do I now not know what relation Yang Jian and Yang Liang are to you?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then issued an edict listing ten crimes and added, "Tell me—what kin are Yang Jian and Yang Liang to you, that you curse them by name?

sentences.zh: 」後乃聽與其子同處。

translations.literal: " Only afterward was he permitted to live together with his son.
translations.idiomatic: Only afterward was he allowed to live with his son.

sentences.zh: 初，楊素嘗以少譴敕送南台，命治書侍御史柳彧治之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang Su had once been sent to the Southern Tribunal by imperial command for a minor fault, and Impeachment Secretary Liu Yu was ordered to try him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yang Su had once been referred to the Southern Tribunal on a minor charge, with Impeachment Secretary Liu Yu assigned to try the case.

sentences.zh: 素恃貴，坐彧床。

translations.literal: Su relied on his rank and sat on Yu's couch.
translations.idiomatic: Su, confident in his high rank, seated himself on Yu's bench.

sentences.zh: 彧從外來見之，於階下端笏整容謂素曰：「奉敕治公之罪！

translations.literal: When Yu came in from outside and saw this, he stood at the foot of the steps, straightened his tablet and his bearing, and said to Su: "I have received command to try your offense!
translations.idiomatic: Yu entered from outside, saw this, and at the foot of the steps straightened his memorial tablet and his bearing. "I bear imperial orders to judge your offense!" he said.

sentences.zh: 」素遽下。

translations.literal: " Su hurriedly rose.
translations.idiomatic: Su scrambled to his feet at once.

sentences.zh: 彧據案而坐，立素於庭，辨詰事狀。

translations.literal: Yu sat at the desk and had Su stand in the courtyard, examining and questioning the facts of the case.
translations.idiomatic: Yu took the judge's seat, made Su stand in the courtyard, and examined the charges against him.

sentences.zh: 素由是銜之。

translations.literal: From this Su bore a grudge against him.
translations.idiomatic: From that day Su nursed a grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 蜀王秀嘗從彧求李文博所撰《治道集》，彧與之；

translations.literal: The Prince of Shu Xiu had once asked Yu for Li Wenbo's Treatise on the Art of Governance, and Yu gave it to him;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shu Xiu had once asked Yu for Li Wenbo's Treatise on the Art of Governance, and Yu lent it to him;

sentences.zh: 秀遺彧奴婢十口。

translations.literal: Xiu presented Yu with ten slave servants.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu repaid him with ten slave servants.

sentences.zh: 及秀得罪，素奏彧以內臣交通諸侯，除名為民，配戍懷遠鎮。

translations.literal: When Xiu fell into guilt, Su memorialized that Yu, as an inner official, had had dealings with feudal lords; he was removed from office and made a commoner, and was assigned to garrison duty at Huaiyuan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu fell, Su accused Yu of improper contact between an inner court official and a territorial prince. Yu was stripped of rank, reduced to common status, and exiled to Huaiyuan Garrison.

sentences.zh: 帝使司農卿趙仲卿往益州窮案秀事，秀之賓客經過之處，仲卿必深文致法，州縣長吏坐者太半。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Minister of Revenue Zhao Zhongqing to Yizhou to exhaustively investigate Xiu's affairs; wherever Xiu's retainers and guests had passed through, Zhongqing invariably twisted the law to the utmost severity, and more than half of the prefectural and county officials were implicated.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Minister of Revenue Zhao Zhongqing to Yizhou to pursue Xiu's case to the fullest. Every place Xiu's guests had touched, Zhongqing stretched the law to its harshest edge, and more than half the local officials were punished.

sentences.zh: 上以為能，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: The Emperor considered him capable and rewarded him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor judged him capable and rewarded him lavishly.

sentences.zh: 久之，貝州長史裴肅遣使上書，稱：「高熲以天挺良才，元勳佐命，為眾所疾，以至廢棄；

translations.literal: After some time, Chief Administrator of Beizhou Pei Su sent an envoy to submit a memorial, stating: "Gao Yong, endowed by Heaven with excellent talent, a founding minister who aided the Mandate, was resented by many and thus came to be cast aside;
translations.idiomatic: After some time, Chief Administrator of Beizhou Pei Su sent a memorial stating, "Gao Yong was Heaven-endowed talent and a founding minister who helped secure the throne, yet envy drove him to ruin;

sentences.zh: 願陛下錄其大功，忘其小過。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will record his great services and forget his small faults.
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to weigh his great service and overlook his minor faults.

sentences.zh: 又二庶人得罪已久，寧無革心！

translations.literal: Moreover, the two commoners have long borne guilt—can they have no change of heart!
translations.idiomatic: The two deposed princes have long been punished—is it not possible they have changed?

sentences.zh: 願陛下弘君父之慈，顧天性之義，各封小國，觀其所為：若能遷善，漸更增益；

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will extend the compassion of ruler and father, heed the righteousness of natural affection, enfeoff each with a small state, and observe their conduct: if they can turn toward goodness, gradually increase their rewards;
translations.idiomatic: Extend a ruler-father's mercy and honor natural affection. Grant each a small fief and watch what they do: if they amend their ways, restore their honors step by step;

sentences.zh: 如或不悛，貶削非晚。

translations.literal: if they do not reform, degradation and reduction will not be late.
translations.idiomatic: if they do not, further punishment can wait.

sentences.zh: 今者自新之路永絕，愧悔之心莫見，豈不哀哉！

translations.literal: Now the path to self-renewal is cut off forever, and no sign of shame or repentance can be seen—is this not pitiable!
translations.idiomatic: As matters stand the road to redemption is closed and no remorse can show itself—is that not pitiable?

sentences.zh: 」書奏，上謂楊素曰：「裴肅憂我家事，此亦至誠也。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor said to Yang Su: "Pei Su is anxious about affairs in my family—this too is utmost sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the Emperor told Yang Su, "Pei Su worries for my house. That is sincere loyalty."

sentences.zh: 」於是征肅入朝。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Pei Su was summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Su was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 太子聞之，謂左庶子張衡曰：「使勇自新，欲何為也？

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince heard of it, he said to Left Palace Companion Zhang Heng: "If Yong is allowed to renew himself, what would that be for?
translations.idiomatic: When the Crown Prince heard, he asked Left Palace Companion Zhang Heng, "If Yong is allowed to reform, what would that mean?

sentences.zh: 」衡曰：「觀肅之意，欲令如吳太伯、漢東海王耳。

translations.literal: " Heng said: "Judging from Su's intent, he wishes to have it as with Wu Taibo or the Prince of Donghai of Han."
translations.idiomatic: Heng replied, "From Su's tone, he means something like Wu Taibo or the Prince of Donghai of Han."

sentences.zh: 」肅至，上面諭以勇不可復收之意而罷遣之。

translations.literal: " When Su arrived, the Emperor personally explained that Yong could not be restored and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Su arrived, the Emperor explained that Yong could not be restored and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 肅，俠之子也。

translations.literal: Su was the son of Pei Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Su was the son of Pei Xia.

sentences.zh: 楊素弟約及從父文思、文紀、族父忌並為尚書、列卿，諸子無汗馬之勞，位至柱國、刺史；

translations.literal: Yang Su's younger brother Yue and his cousins Wensi, Wenji, and his clansman uncle Ji all served as Ministers and chief ministers; his sons, without labor of horseback in war, rose to ranks of Pillar of State and regional governors;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su's brother Yue, his cousins Wensi and Wenji, and his clansman uncle Ji all held ministerial posts; his sons, without ever sweating in the saddle, rose to be Pillars of State and regional governors;

sentences.zh: 廣營資產，自京師及諸方都會處，邸店、碾磑、便利田宅，不可勝數；

translations.literal: They broadly accumulated assets; from the capital to every major market city, inns, shops, grain mills, oil presses, and profitable fields and houses were beyond counting;
translations.idiomatic: The family amassed property on every side: in the capital and in every major market, inns, shops, mills, presses, and profitable estates beyond counting;

sentences.zh: 家僮數千，後庭妓妾曳綺羅者以千數；

translations.literal: household slaves numbered in the thousands, and singing girls and concubines in the rear chambers trailing in brocade and gauze numbered in the thousands;
translations.idiomatic: household slaves ran to the thousands, and rear-garden concubines and entertainers draped in silk numbered a thousand or more;

sentences.zh: 第宅華侈，制擬宮禁；

translations.literal: mansions were luxurious and extravagant, their regulations modeled on the palace precincts;
translations.idiomatic: their mansions rivaled the palace in splendor and regulation;

sentences.zh: 親故吏布列清顯。

translations.literal: relatives, old associates, and subordinates were stationed throughout honored and prominent posts.
translations.idiomatic: kinsmen, old allies, and former subordinates filled the most visible offices in the realm.

sentences.zh: 既廢一太子及一王，威權愈盛。

translations.literal: Having already deposed one Crown Prince and one prince, his power and authority grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: After the deposition of one crown prince and one prince, his power only grew.

sentences.zh: 朝臣有違忤者，或至誅夷；

translations.literal: Court officials who opposed him might even be executed and their clans exterminated;
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers who crossed him might be executed to the last kin;

sentences.zh: 有附會及親戚，雖無才用，必加進擢，朝廷靡然，莫不畏附。

translations.literal: those who attached themselves to him and his kinsmen, though without talent or ability, were invariably advanced and promoted; the court inclined toward him, and none did not fear and attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: cronies and relatives, however worthless, were promoted without fail, until the court bent to him and none dared stand apart.

sentences.zh: 敢與素抗而不橈者，獨柳彧及尚書右丞李綱、大理卿梁毘而已。

translations.literal: Those who dared resist Su without bending were only Liu Yu, Vice Minister of the Right Li Gang, and Chief Judge of Justice Liang Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Only Liu Yu, Vice Minister Li Gang, and Chief Judge of Justice Liang Bi dared oppose him without yielding.

sentences.zh: 始，毘為西寧州刺史，凡十一年，蠻夷酋長皆以金多者為豪雋，遞相攻奪，略無寧歲，毘患之。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Bi was Governor of Xining Prefecture—for eleven years in all—the tribal chieftains all regarded whoever had the most gold as the leading hero, attacking and seizing from one another in turn, with scarcely a peaceful year; Bi was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: Bi had served eleven years as governor of Xining, where tribal chiefs measured prestige in gold and raided one another year after year. The endless violence troubled him deeply.

sentences.zh: 後因諸酋長相帥以金遺毘，毘置金坐側，對之慟哭，而謂之曰：「此物饑不可食，寒不可衣，汝等以此相滅，不可勝數，今將此來，欲殺我邪！

translations.literal: Later, when the chieftains together came bearing gold as gifts to Bi, Bi placed the gold beside his seat, wept bitterly before it, and said to them: "This stuff cannot be eaten when hungry or worn when cold; you destroy one another over it beyond counting; now you bring it to me—do you wish to kill me!
translations.idiomatic: When the chiefs came together to present him with gold, Bi set the metal beside his seat and wept before them. "This cannot feed hunger or ward off cold," he said.
