"You have slaughtered one another over it beyond count. Do you bring it to me now intending to kill me as well?

sentences.zh: 」一無所納。

translations.literal: " He accepted nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: He refused every gift.

sentences.zh: 於是蠻夷感悟，遂不相攻擊。

translations.literal: Thereupon the barbarians and tribes were moved to understanding and no longer attacked one another.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes were shamed into peace and ceased their raids.

sentences.zh: 上聞而善之，征為大理卿，處法平允。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of it he approved, summoned him to serve as Chief Judge of Justice, and he handled the law with fairness and equity.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised his conduct, recalled him to serve as Chief Judge of Justice, and Bi administered the law with evenhanded fairness.

sentences.zh: 毘見楊素專權，恐為國患，乃上封事曰：「臣聞臣無有作威作福，其害於而家，凶於而國。

translations.literal: Bi saw that Yang Su monopolized power and feared he would become a peril to the state; he therefore submitted a sealed memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that when ministers presume to wield might and dispense blessings on their own authority, it is harmful to their house and ruinous to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Yang Su's monopoly on power, Bi feared for the realm and submitted a sealed memorial: "I have read that when ministers wield arbitrary power and dispense arbitrary favor, their houses are harmed and the state brought to ruin.

sentences.zh: 竊見左僕射越國公素，幸遇愈重，權勢日隆，搢紳之徒，屬其視聽。

translations.literal: I have privately observed that Left Pushe, Duke of Yue Su, enjoys ever greater favor, his power and influence daily ascend, and the gentry attach themselves to his sight and hearing.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that Left Pushe, Duke of Yue Yang Su, enjoys ever greater imperial favor; his power grows daily, and officials everywhere watch his eyes and ears for direction.

sentences.zh: 忤旨者嚴霜夏零，阿旨者甘雨冬澍；

translations.literal: Those who defied his will met with harsh frost falling in summer; those who flattered his will received sweet rain moistening in winter;
translations.idiomatic: Those who defied him met withering frost in midsummer; those who flattered him found sweet rain in deep winter;

sentences.zh: 榮枯由其脣吻，廢興候其指麾；

translations.literal: glory and withering depended on his lips and tongue; dismissal and advancement awaited his finger and command;
translations.idiomatic: careers rose or fell on his word alone, and fortunes waited upon his gesture;

sentences.zh: 所私皆非忠讜，所進鹹是親戚，子弟布列，兼州連縣。

translations.literal: those he favored were none loyal and straightforward; those he advanced were all kinsmen; sons and younger brothers were deployed everywhere, holding several prefectures and linked counties.
translations.idiomatic: his favorites were none of them honest advisers; his promotions were all relatives; sons and brothers held posts across province after province;

sentences.zh: 天下無事，容息異圖；

translations.literal: While all under Heaven is at peace, he may harbor other designs at leisure;
translations.idiomatic: in peacetime he may already be nursing other designs;

sentences.zh: 四海有虞，必為禍始。

translations.literal: when the four seas have cause for anxiety, he will surely be the origin of calamity.
translations.idiomatic: in crisis he would surely be the source of disaster.

sentences.zh: 夫奸臣擅命，有漸而來，王莽資之於積年，桓玄基之於易世，而卒殄漢祀，終傾晉祚。

translations.literal: Now, wicked ministers who usurp command come by gradual steps: Wang Mang built on years of accumulation, Huan Xuan laid foundations at a change of era—yet in the end they extinguished Han's sacrifices and toppled Jin's Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Usurpers do not appear overnight: Wang Mang built his power over many years, Huan Xuan seized his moment at a dynastic turn—and both in the end destroyed their dynasties.

sentences.zh: 陛下若以素為阿衡，臣恐其心未必伊尹也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty treats Su as an Aheng, I fear his heart may not be that of an Yi Yin.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would make Su your Aheng—the regent at your right hand—I doubt his heart is truly that of an Yi Yin.

sentences.zh: 伏願揆鑒古今，量為處置，俾洪基永固，率土幸甚！

translations.literal: I humbly pray that Your Majesty weigh the past and present, measure and dispose accordingly, so that the great foundation may stand forever and all within the realm may be greatly blessed!
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to weigh past and present, act as the times require, and so keep the dynasty's foundation secure—a blessing to every subject under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」書奏，上大怒，收毘繫獄，親詰之。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, the emperor was greatly enraged, had Bi arrested and imprisoned, and personally interrogated him.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached him, the emperor flew into a rage, had Bi arrested and thrown into prison, and questioned him in person.

sentences.zh: 毘極言「素擅寵弄權，將領之處，殺戮無道。

translations.literal: Bi spoke to the utmost, saying: "Su monopolizes favor and manipulates power; wherever he commands troops, he kills without principle.
translations.idiomatic: Bi held nothing back: "Su hoards imperial favor and twists power to his own ends. Wherever he holds command, men die by his whim, without justice or restraint.

sentences.zh: 又太子、蜀王罪廢之日，百僚無不震竦，唯素揚眉奮肘，喜見容色，利國家有事以為身幸。

translations.literal: Moreover, on the day the Crown Prince and the Prince of Shu were condemned and deposed, not one among the hundred officials failed to tremble in fear—only Su raised his brows and flexed his elbows, joy plain on his face, treating trouble for the state as good fortune for himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the Crown Prince and the Prince of Shu were deposed, every official at court trembled—every official but Su, who lifted his brows and squared his elbows, delight written on his face, as though the nation's crisis were his private windfall.

sentences.zh: 」上無以屈，乃釋之。

translations.literal: " The emperor had no means to refute him, and so released him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not gainsay him, and let him go.

sentences.zh: 其後上亦浸疏忌素，乃下敕曰：「僕射國之宰輔，不可躬親細務，但三五日一向省，評論大事。

translations.literal: Afterward the emperor also gradually grew distant from and suspicious of Su, and issued an edict saying: "The Vice Premier is the state's chief minister; he must not personally attend to petty affairs, but need only come to the office once every few days to review and discuss great matters.
translations.idiomatic: After that the emperor grew steadily cooler toward Su and more wary of him. He issued an edict: "The Vice Premier is the state's foremost minister. He must not bury himself in routine business; let him come to court only every few days to deliberate on weighty affairs.

sentences.zh: 」外示優崇，實奪之權也。

translations.literal: " Outwardly this showed honor and elevation; in reality it stripped him of power.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly it was honor; in truth it was the withdrawal of his authority.

sentences.zh: 素由是終仁壽之末，不復通判省事。

translations.literal: Su therefore, to the end of the Renshou era, no longer reviewed and decided administrative matters.
translations.idiomatic: From then until the close of the Renshou reign, Su no longer handled day-to-day governance at all.

sentences.zh: 出楊約為伊州刺史。

translations.literal: Yang Yue was sent out as Governor of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yue was posted away as governor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 素既被疏，吏部尚書柳述益用事，攝兵部尚書，參掌機密；

translations.literal: Once Su had been distanced, Minister of Personnel Liu Shu came increasingly into power, acting concurrently as Minister of War and sharing in confidential affairs;
translations.idiomatic: With Su sidelined, Minister of Personnel Liu Shu gained ground. He doubled as acting Minister of War and was admitted to the inner circle of state secrets;

sentences.zh: 素由是惡之。

translations.literal: Su therefore hated him.
translations.idiomatic: and Su came to hate him for it.

sentences.zh: 太子問於賀若弼曰：「楊素、韓擒虎、史萬歲皆稱良將，其優劣何如？

translations.literal: The Crown Prince asked He Ruobi: "Yang Su, Han Qinhu, and Shi Wansui are all called fine generals—how do they compare in merit?
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince asked He Ruobi, "Yang Su, Han Qinhu, and Shi Wansui are all praised as fine generals. How do they rank against one another?

sentences.zh: 」弼曰：「楊素猛將，非謀將；

translations.literal: " Bi replied: "Yang Su is a fierce general, not a strategist;
translations.idiomatic: Ruobi answered, "Yang Su is a fierce fighter, not a strategist;

sentences.zh: 韓擒虎鬥將，非領將；

translations.literal: Han Qinhu is a duelist general, not a commander;
translations.idiomatic: Han Qinhu is a brawler on the field, not a man to lead armies;

sentences.zh: 史萬歲騎將，非大將。

translations.literal: Shi Wansui is a cavalry general, not a great commander.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wansui is a cavalryman, not a commander of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 」太子曰：「然則大將誰也？

translations.literal: " The Crown Prince said: "Then who is the great commander?
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince asked, "Then who is the great commander?

sentences.zh: 」弼拜曰：「唯殿下所擇！

translations.literal: " Bi bowed and said: "Only Your Highness may choose!
translations.idiomatic: Ruobi bowed low. "That, Highness, is for you alone to decide!

sentences.zh: 」弼意自許也。

translations.literal: " Bi meant this as self-praise.
translations.idiomatic: He meant himself, of course.

sentences.zh: 交州俚帥李佛子作亂，據越王故城，遣其兄子大權據龍編城，其別帥李普鼎據烏延城。

translations.literal: Li Fozi, a Li chieftain of Jiaozhou, rebelled, holding the former city of the King of Yue; he sent his elder brother's son Daquan to hold Longbian City, while another chieftain, Li Puding, held Wuyan City.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaozhou the Li chieftain Li Fozi rose in rebellion, seizing the old capital of the King of Yue. He sent his brother's son Daquan to hold Longbian while a subordinate chief, Li Puding, took Wuyan.

sentences.zh: 楊素薦瓜州刺史長安劉方有將帥之略，詔以方為交州道行軍總管，統二十七營而進。

translations.literal: Yang Su recommended Liu Fang of Chang'an, Governor of Guazhou, as having the capacity of a commander, and an edict appointed Fang campaigning commander of the Jiaozhou route, leading twenty-seven camps forward.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su recommended Liu Fang of Chang'an, governor of Guazhou, as a man of real command. The emperor made him campaigning commander on the Jiaozhou route at the head of twenty-seven battalions.

sentences.zh: 方軍令嚴肅，有犯必斬；

translations.literal: Fang's military discipline was severe; any violation was punished by beheading;
translations.idiomatic: Fang ran a tight army: any breach of discipline meant the headsman's block;

sentences.zh: 然仁愛士卒，有疾病者親臨撫親，士卒亦以此懷之。

translations.literal: yet he loved his soldiers tenderly, and when any fell ill he personally came to tend them; the troops therefore cherished him for this.
translations.idiomatic: yet he cared for his men, and when any fell sick he nursed them himself. The soldiers loved him for it.

sentences.zh: 至都隆嶺，遇賊，擊破之。

translations.literal: When they reached Dulong Ridge they encountered the rebels and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At Dulong Ridge they met the rebels and broke them.

sentences.zh: 進軍臨佛子營，先諭以禍福。

translations.literal: Advancing, the army came before Fozi's camp and first explained fortune and disaster to him.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing on to Fozi's camp, Fang first sent word of the rewards of surrender and the cost of resistance.

sentences.zh: 佛子懼，請降，送之長安。

translations.literal: Fozi was afraid, requested surrender, and was sent to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Fozi, terrified, submitted and was escorted to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，壬申，賜幽州總管燕榮死。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, on the day renshen, Yan Rong, Regional Commander of Youzhou, was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on renshen day, Yan Rong, regional commander of Youzhou, was condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 榮性嚴酷，鞭撻左右，動至千數。

translations.literal: Rong's nature was harsh and cruel; he flogged those around him, often reaching a thousand strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was savage by nature. He beat his attendants until the lash count ran into the thousands.

sentences.zh: 嘗見道次叢荊，以為堪作杖，命取之，輒以試人。

translations.literal: Once, seeing thorn bushes by the roadside, he thought they would make fine rods, ordered them taken, and immediately tried them on people.
translations.idiomatic: Once, passing a roadside thicket, he decided the thorns would make excellent rods, had them cut, and at once tested them on whoever was at hand.

sentences.zh: 人或自陳無罪，榮曰：「後有罪，當免汝。

translations.literal: When someone pleaded that he was guiltless, Rong said: "If you commit an offense later, I shall pardon you.
translations.idiomatic: When a man protested his innocence, Rong said, "Commit a crime later and I'll let you off then.

sentences.zh: 」既而有犯，將杖之，人曰：「前日被杖，使君許以有罪宥之。

translations.literal: " Later, when the man did offend and was about to be beaten, the man said: "The other day you beat me and promised that if I had an offense you would pardon me.
translations.idiomatic: When the same man did offend and the rod was raised again, he reminded Rong: "You beat me the other day and promised a pardon if I ever broke the law.

sentences.zh: 」榮曰：「無罪尚爾，況有罪邪！

translations.literal: " Rong said: "When you were guiltless I still beat you—how much more when you are guilty!
translations.idiomatic: Rong replied, "I flogged you when you were innocent. Do you think I'd spare you now that you're guilty?

sentences.zh: 」杖之自若。

translations.literal: " He had him beaten just the same.
translations.idiomatic: And he beat him all the same.

sentences.zh: 觀州長史元弘嗣遷幽州長史，懼為榮所辱，固辭。

translations.literal: Yuan Hongsi, Long Secretary of Guanzhou, was transferred to Long Secretary of Youzhou; fearing humiliation at Rong's hands, he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hongsi, long secretary of Guanzhou, was reassigned as long secretary of Youzhou. Dreading Rong's abuse, he refused the post outright.

sentences.zh: 上敕榮曰：「弘嗣杖十已上罪，皆須奏聞。

translations.literal: The emperor commanded Rong: "For any offense of Hongsi warranting more than ten strokes of the rod, you must report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instructed Rong: "For any offense by Hongsi calling for more than ten strokes, you must first report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 」榮忿曰：「豎子何敢玩我！

translations.literal: " Rong said in anger: "What does this stripling dare to make sport of me!
translations.idiomatic: Rong snarled, "Who does this whelp think he is, playing me for a fool!

sentences.zh: 」於是遣弘嗣監納倉粟，揚得一糠一秕，皆罰之。

translations.literal: " He therefore sent Hongsi to supervise the intake of granary grain; if a single husk or empty grain was found in the winnowing, he was punished.
translations.idiomatic: He put Hongsi in charge of receiving granary grain and fined him for every speck of chaff or hollow kernel in the winnow.

sentences.zh: 每笞雖不滿十，然一日之中，或至三數。

translations.literal: Though each beating was fewer than ten strokes, within a single day there might be two or three rounds.
translations.idiomatic: No single beating exceeded ten strokes, yet two or three floggings in one day were common.

sentences.zh: 如是歷年，怨隙日構。

translations.literal: Thus for years, resentment and rift grew day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year the hatred between them deepened.

sentences.zh: 榮遂收弘嗣付獄，禁絕其糧，弘嗣抽衣絮雜水咽之。

translations.literal: Rong then had Hongsi arrested and put in prison, cutting off his food; Hongsi pulled stuffing from his clothes, mixed it with water, and swallowed it.
translations.idiomatic: At last Rong jailed Hongsi and cut off his rations. Hongsi soaked scraps of cloth from his garments in water and swallowed them to stay alive.

sentences.zh: 其妻詣闕稱冤，上遣使按驗，奏榮暴虐，贓穢狼籍；

translations.literal: His wife went to the palace to plead her grievance; the emperor sent an envoy to investigate, who reported that Rong was brutal and tyrannical and that his corruption was flagrant;
translations.idiomatic: His wife appealed at court. The emperor sent investigators, who reported Rong's cruelty and brazen corruption;

sentences.zh: 征還，賜死。

translations.literal: he was recalled and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was recalled and condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 元弘嗣代榮為政。

translations.literal: Yuan Hongsi took over Rong's administration.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hongsi succeeded him in office.

sentences.zh: 酷又甚之。

translations.literal: His cruelty was even worse.
translations.idiomatic: He was crueler still.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬戌，置常平官。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on the day renxu, Ever-Normal Granary officials were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renxu day, the Ever-Normal Granary offices were established.

sentences.zh: 是歲，龍門王通詣闕獻《太平十二策》，上不能用，罷歸。

translations.literal: That year, Wang Tong of Longmen came to court and presented the Twelve Policies for Great Peace; the emperor could not employ them, and Tong was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wang Tong of Longmen came to court with his Twelve Policies for Great Peace. The emperor took no use of them, and Tong returned home unrewarded.

sentences.zh: 通遂教授於河、汾之間，弟子自遠至者甚眾，累征不起。

translations.literal: Tong then taught between the Yellow and Fen Rivers; disciples came from afar in great numbers, and though repeatedly summoned he would not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He settled to teach between the Yellow and Fen Rivers. Students flocked to him from distant places, and though the court summoned him again and again, he never entered service.

sentences.zh: 楊素甚重之，勸之仕，通曰：「通有先人之弊廬足以蔽風雨，薄田足以具{衍食}粥，讀書談道足以自樂。

translations.literal: Yang Su greatly esteemed him and urged him to take office; Tong said: "Tong has his forebears' humble dwelling, enough to shelter from wind and rain, and thin fields enough to provide porridge; reading and discussing the Way are enough for his own joy.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su held him in high regard and pressed him to serve. Tong replied, "I have my ancestors' humble roof, enough to keep off wind and rain, and a small plot enough for gruel. Books and talk of the Way are pleasure enough for me.

sentences.zh: 願明公正身以治天下，使時和歲豐，通也受賜多矣，不願仕也。

translations.literal: I only wish that the Duke would rectify himself and govern the realm, so that the times are harmonious and the harvests rich—then Tong would receive great benefit, and does not wish to take office.
translations.idiomatic: What I ask is that you govern the realm with an upright heart, so that peace reigns and harvests abound. That would be gift enough for me. I have no wish to serve.

sentences.zh: 」或譖通於素曰：「彼實慢公，公何敬焉？

translations.literal: " Someone slandered Tong to Su, saying: "He in truth treats the Duke lightly—why do you honor him?
translations.idiomatic: Someone whispered to Su that Tong was secretly mocking him: "He looks down on you—why do you treat him with such respect?

sentences.zh: 」素以問通，通曰：「使公可慢，則僕得矣；

translations.literal: " Su asked Tong about it; Tong said: "If the Duke could be treated lightly, then I would gain;
translations.idiomatic: Su put the charge to Tong himself. Tong answered, "If you were a man one could treat lightly, I would be the better for it;

sentences.zh: 不可慢，則僕失矣：得失在僕，公何預焉！

translations.literal: if he cannot be treated lightly, then I would lose: gain and loss rest with me—what has the Duke to do with it!
translations.idiomatic: if you are not such a man, then I lose. The gain or loss is mine alone—what has that to do with you?

sentences.zh: 」素待之如初。

translations.literal: " Su treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: Su treated him just as he had before.

sentences.zh: 弟子賈瓊問息謗，通曰：「無辯。

translations.literal: The disciple Jia Qiong asked how to still slander; Tong said: "Do not argue.
translations.idiomatic: His student Jia Qiong asked how to silence slander. Tong said, "Do not argue.

sentences.zh: 」問止怨，曰：「不爭。

translations.literal: " Asked how to stop resentment, he said: "Do not contend.
translations.idiomatic: Asked how to end resentment, he said, "Do not contend.

sentences.zh: 」通嘗稱：「無赦之國，其刑必平；

translations.literal: " Tong once declared: "In a state without amnesties, punishments will surely be even;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tong once said, "In a realm that grants no pardons, punishments will be evenhanded;

sentences.zh: 重斂之國，其財必削。

translations.literal: in a state of heavy exactions, its wealth will surely be drained.
translations.idiomatic: in a realm of heavy levies, its wealth will surely be drained.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「聞謗而怒者，讒之□也；

translations.literal: " He also said: "One who grows angry upon hearing slander is the decoy of slander;
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "He who flies into a rage at slander becomes the decoy of slander;

sentences.zh: 見譽而喜者，佞之媒也；

translations.literal: one who grows glad upon seeing praise is the go-between of flattery;
translations.idiomatic: he who brightens at praise becomes the go-between of flattery;

sentences.zh: 絕□去媒，讒佞遠矣。

translations.literal: cut off the decoy and remove the go-between, and slander and flattery will be far away.
translations.idiomatic: cut off the decoy and dismiss the go-between, and slander and flattery will keep their distance.

sentences.zh: 」大業末，卒於家，門人謚曰文中子。

translations.literal: " At the end of the Daye era he died at home; his disciples gave him the posthumous title Master Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Daye reign he died at home. His disciples gave him the posthumous title Master Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 突厥步迦可汗所部大亂，鐵勒僕骨等十餘部，皆叛步迦降於啟民。

translations.literal: The tribes under Tardu Khan of the Turks fell into great disorder; more than ten tribes of the Tiele, including Pugu, all rebelled against Tardu and submitted to Qimin.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes under the Turkish khan Tardu fell into chaos. More than ten Tiele tribes, Pugu among them, broke from Tardu and submitted to Qimin.

sentences.zh: 步迦眾潰，西奔吐谷渾；

translations.literal: Tardu's forces collapsed and fled west to Tuyuhun;
translations.idiomatic: Tardu's army disintegrated and fled west toward Tuyuhun;

sentences.zh: 長孫晟送啟民置磧口，啟民於是盡有步迦之眾。

translations.literal: Changsun Sheng escorted Qimin to the desert pass, and Qimin thereby came to hold all of Tardu's followers.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Sheng installed Qimin at the desert pass, and Qimin thereby absorbed all of Tardu's people.
